Scotland begin their Nations League campaign with the visit to Slovenia on 26 September. Pocognoli’s first home game in charge will be Switzerland’s visit to Glasgow three days later.

Sports.title: Women’s U20 World Cup boycott may hurt in short term but can send Fifa a vital message | Tom Garry
Sports.content:
“And I say to all the women … Pick the right battles. Pick the right fights. You have the power to change. You have the power to convince us men what we have to do and what we don’t have to do. You do it. Just do it. With men, with Fifa, you will find open doors. Just push the doors. They are open.”

Those were the condescending words of Fifa’s president, Gianni Infantino, three years ago during a tone-deaf speech in Sydney, which left his audience, including some of the most senior women in the game, exasperated. It is a damning indictment of Infantino’s tenure that his patronising monologue on the eve of the Women’s World Cup final now barely even creeps into the top 10 of the most controversial moments since his latest re-election, in March 2023.

Yet, with the Swiss administrator’s future hanging finely in the balance, the power to enforce once-in-a-generation change at Fifa may well be in the hands of women’s teams after all, as the threat of a boycott lingers over September’s Women’s Under-20 World Cup, the Women’s Under-17 World Cup, which gets under way in October, and that month’s senior World Cup playoff ties for next summer’s major showpiece, the Women’s World Cup in Brazil.

This week Lisa Nandy told the BBC that Infantino “should go” and, overall, the culture secretary spoke well on the matter, but she added that she would not support a boycott of the U20 World Cup and said she was “not generally in favour of sporting boycotts full stop – because they unfairly penalise athletes and competitors who are not responsible for the reason that these boycotts take place”. On that specific element, it is important to respectfully disagree with Nandy and the many others who share that view.

Yes, it would feel deeply unjust for football’s political turmoil to have an adverse impact on the development of the world’s best young women footballers through no fault of their own, but that is why any participating countries being prepared to boycott the upcoming under-20 tournament would send such a powerful message.

It is tempting to follow the stance that many working within the women’s game are taking privately, which is that it would be a travesty if women’s football, having been neglected and let down by the authorities for generations, was harmed again by disruption to such a significant tournament, but the painful reality is that the young generation of women’s stars stand to be most affected by the decisions that are made by governing bodies in the days, weeks and months ahead.

View image in fullscreen North Korea celebrate winning the most recent Women’s U20 World Cup, in 2024. Photograph: Julian Medina/SPP/Shutterstock

And yes, is it unfair for women’s teams, and young women’s teams in particular, to shoulder the responsibility of taking a stance against the now-scrapped vision of selling off a stake in Fifa tournaments – which, we should remember, would include all Fifa’s women’s tournaments too – through the murky concept of the Fifa Forward Enterprise subsidiary, but it is their futures, and the organisation of the World Cups finals that will come to define their careers, which are at stake.

And the future of the governance of the sport, and decisions about who runs the game, is a debate that women’s football players, coaches and fans all deserve a much more vocal say in, on far more deep-rooted injustices than those that have dominated the news in recent weeks.

Is it fair that, for example, there are only two women – Paola López of Mexico and Vietnam’s Thi My Dung Nguyen – among the 18 members of Fifa’s disciplinary committee, which hit the headlines amid the farcical Folarin Balogun scandal this summer? Or that all 10 of the members of Fifa’s Future of Football committee are men?

Is it fair that, of the 37 members of Fifa’s council, the organisation’s strategic and oversight body, 29 are men and only eight are women? Or that seven of the eight vice-presidents are men?

Is it fair that the 2023 Women’s World Cup prize money totalled $110m and this summer’s men’s World Cup’s prize pot was around eight times larger, at a record-breaking $871m?

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

It would be wrong to say that there have not been positive improvements in women’s football across the world since Infantino took office in 2016. The past decade has included long overdue, albeit still very important and welcome, enhancements to provisions for players and coaches at women’s tournaments, a sizeable growth in financial investment and huge uplift in prize money, albeit from a very low bar. It is also fair to say that there are many key figures in the women’s game, across all continents, who support Infantino and are appreciative of the gradual improvements that are being made, while acknowledging that there is still a very long way to go.

View image in fullscreen Lucy Bronze has backed a boycott. Photograph: Mike Egerton/PA

But everyone associated with women’s football should be concerned that the 25-page sales pitch that was titled Fifa Forward Enterprise Member Materials contained only one token reference to women’s football. It is why the England defender Lucy Bronze was right to use her voice to say she backed a boycott “for the good of the game”.

On Friday morning, the latest twist in Infantino’s future delivered both positives and negatives for the under-fire president, as on the one hand, the Oceania Football Confederation declared its support for Infantino, while the confederation’s biggest member, New Zealand, withdrew its backing for him. New Zealand, impeccable co-hosts of the most recent Women’s World Cup, will have had plenty of reasons to support Infantino but has chosen to use its platform to call for “stronger governance, accountability and transparency”.

Shortly before that news, on Thursday, a feature article was published on Fifa’s website entitled “Europe’s finest hours at the Under-20 Women’s World Cup”, looking back at dazzling performances of young breakthrough stars such as Spain’s Salma Paralluelo’s in 2022 or the Germany striker Alexandra Popp in 2010. Next month six European teams – including the hosts, Poland – are scheduled to show the world what they are capable of, but – whether the timing of that article was purely coincidental, political or ironic – European women’s under-20 teams’ finest hour may still be yet to come.

Sports.title: London City Lionesses’ Mapi León: ‘It is a club created for women. It is beautiful and exciting’
Sports.content:
‘No, I can’t, I’m sorry, it’s a secret!” Mapi León roars with laughter, in response to being asked what persuaded her to join London City Lionesses. Does this bode badly for our interview? Fear not, the Spain centre-back is in as banterous and jovial a mood as you could imagine any new signing to be, as she embarks on her first major interview since signing for the Women’s Super League club.

Across the course of our conversation, in bright sunshine outside a quiet hotel near Maidstone, it is evident that the 31-year-old could scarcely be happier about her decision to swap Barcelona for south-east England. She is sorely missing her cat, Bagheera (“Here, you ask for so many things for pets, you can’t [really] fly with them, it’s so many documents, so many things”) but, that aside, she is buoyant, relaxed and clearly embracing English life. She says she likes the “little bread” in the morning, and we eventually establish she is referring to crumpets, and reveals: “I like the beans in the morning. It’s really interesting. My Spanish teammates like Alexia [Putellas] and Jana [Fernández] are like: ‘What are you doing eating beans in the morning? You need to train.’ I go: ‘No, it’s fine I like it.’”

However, English breakfasts were surely not what attracted her to Kent to play for London City Lionesses so, returning to that first question, she explains thoughtfully: “My body was craving something different. I spent many years in a comfortable position, because playing at Barça has been absolutely wonderful and very nice; it is a style of game that suits me a lot and coming to England, the football is very different from the Spanish one, at first glance. So, I think [the reason was] being able to challenge myself and see if I am capable. I am going to make an effort to adapt to this league and also to show myself that I’m able to compete in another style of play that is not the one that makes me stand out the most.”

An undisputed club legend at Barcelona, León certainly stood out in Spain as the best ball-playing centre-back of her generation, and won seven league titles, seven Copa de la Reina’s and – most impressively – four Champions League titles, during a nine-year period of relentless dominance with Barcelona, whom she joined from Atlético Madrid in 2017.

Allow Instagram content? This article includes content provided by Instagram . We ask for your permission before anything is loaded, as they may be using cookies and other technologies. To view this content, click 'Allow and continue'. Allow and continue

This summer she was one of four members of the Spain starting XI that beat England 4-0 in June in Mallorca to leave Barcelona, together with Arsenal’s new signing Ona Batlle, OL Lyonnes’ new winger Salma Paralluelo and, most notably, her London City Lionesses teammate Alexia Putellas. Together, León and Putellas drew raised eyebrows across the women’s game by swapping the reigning European champions for a lesser-known team that finished sixth in the WSL last term, but they have been joined by a series of other world-renowned names including the former England goalkeeper Mary Earps and the France winger Kadidiatou Diani.

The club’s new signings meet the vision of their ambitious owner, the American businesswoman Michele Kang, of whom León says: “The impression I get is of an empowered woman, with a winning mindset, driven by a desire to see things improve and a drive to win. And that is a competitive and winning mentality. And if in the end, I want to be part of it because it is a club created for women and that is not common, I think it is beautiful and exciting.

“Everything counts when you make this kind of a decision, and of course, [Kang] was an important part because seeing another woman doing so much to help women’s sports, and women’s football grow, I think it’s impossible not to value that. I think it’s something very powerful.”

View image in fullscreen Mapi León hugs the Champions League trophy after Barcelona’s victory over Wolfsburg in 2023, the second of four WCL titles the defender had won with the club. Photograph: Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty Images

The club’s signings of Putellas and León were announced five days apart in July, which prompts the question: did they discuss their decision with one another and was it a case of “If you go, I’ll go too”?

“No, not really, no. I think we take the issue of personal matters very seriously,” León says. “It’s a very different challenge. You come from a league where you win every year. Where you have achieved great things internationally and you come to a club that finished mid-table with some different challenges. And I think it is a very personal decision for each individual to make, choosing what is best for you personally.

“[You ask yourself] what do you really need right now? What is your body telling you? What do you think is best for you to keep improving, to keep pushing yourself, and to maintain that ambition? And I think each person needs different things. So, there wasn’t much communication between us. And that the decision wasn’t planned.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The more she reflects on her move, the tactical differences between Liga F and the WSL become clear as a key factor, as the Zaragoza-born defender continues: “The English league can give me a lot. You can learn a lot. The transitions, the style of play, playing with more space. The pressing is different too because I’m used to teams often sitting back in a mid-to-low block, whereas here, it’s probably more of a high press. I’d like to bring a bit of calm to the game.

“I don’t know if that really fits with English football, but no, of course, I don’t want to change the system, but simply the timings as a centre-back. I am a centre-back so I see everything. And I like to control a little bit of the timings so maybe we can try to have a little bit more of the ball. Or there are many spaces, so we can go. So I like to have a bit of control.

View image in fullscreen Mapi León is one of several big summer signings made by London City Lionesses and was attracted by the competitive nature of the WSL. Photograph: Sally Rawlins/London City Lionesses

“The league is so competitive, the commitment the league is making, the clubs, I mean, I think everything makes it very attractive to come because I have been following the English league over these years and it feels like it can’t let you relax even for a second, not in any match, not during the match. Not a single second can relax you, because the English league is much more competitive.”

Her new side open the season at home to Manchester United on 4 September. Until then, she is embracing a comparatively quiet life and enjoying not being recognised in public, adding: “It’s so different [here]. It’s not a bad thing but, I can just walk to buy food, and no one recognises me! And sometimes it’s nice, because in Barcelona we are not ‘famous’ but people know us. It’s one of the many amazing things. But also sometimes you miss this freedom. Like, just go and shop.”

How long that newfound anonymity will continue is hard to tell, as it will surely not take long for León to become one of the most recognisable faces in the WSL if she can bring her form for Spain and Barcelona straight to London City Lionesses. For now, she can enjoy her beans and her crumpets in peace.

Sports.title: Arsenal FA Cup winner retires aged 34 – months after being released by League One side
Sports.content:
Arsenal FA Cup winner retires aged 34 – months after being released by League One side

Former Arsenal and West Ham defender Carl Jenkinson has announced his retirement from football at the age of 34.

The 2014 FA Cup winner was part of Bromley's League Two promotion-winning squad last season, but was released earlier this summer.

5 Jenkinson made three appearances in Arsenal's 2013/14 FA Cup-winning campaign Credit: Getty

Jenkinson, who earned one senior cap for England - featuring for Roy Hodgson's Three Lions against Sweden in 2012 - joined Bromley in September 2024.

But he battled injury setbacks during his time at Hayes Lane, with the right-back featuring in just 13 matches in his opening season.

And he was restricted to just five League Two outings last campaign as Bromley won the title to secure their place in England's third-tier.

In a lengthy statement confirming his retirement on social media, Jenksinon confessed to struggling with confidence issues throughout his career.

What did Carl Jenkisnon say in his retirement statement?

He posted on X: "Thank you to everyone who played a part in my journey, from my Charlton days as a kid through to my last time playing football at Bromley.

"From the age of eight, football has been my life, it’s given me a lot, and I have also given it a lot back. In fact I’ve given it everything."

"It’s for that reason that I can write this looking back over my career with no regrets. Do I wish certain things went better? Without a doubt.

"A lot of things. I once scored an own goal from 30 yards out. I certainly wouldn’t mind deleting that from history.

"But were these bad or difficult moments ever because of a lack of effort? No. Like I said, I gave football everything. Everyday.

"And I guess I’m writing this because I can see that’s getting lost a bit these days.

5 Jenkinson was released by Bromley after just less than two years at the club Credit: Getty

"I don’t know if it’s social media painting a certain picture of what a footballer looks like, but I want to be clear, behind the scenes these top players train like their life depends on it.

"Alexis Sanchez, wow. Every training session he trained like it was his last. The ones that don’t, they fall by the way side eventually.

"Even when they’re really, really good. I’ve seen it happen to too many young pros and scholars, trying to make a name in the game.

"Apply yourself everyday, listen to your coaches and learn from the players who have already been where you want to get to.

"Because if you don’t make it, and it’s because you got carried away with yourself, it’ll be a heavy burden to carry later in life.

"I suffered a lot with confidence throughout my career, which I found strange because my Dad always backs himself to the hilt.

5 Jenkinson scored once for Arsenal from his 70 appearances across all competitions Credit: Getty

5 His fine form at the start of the 2012/13 season saw him rewarded with his one and only England cap Credit: Getty

"I saw loads of people, to try and unlock something within me and find that inner belief. 'Take the chains off,' Arsene Wenger would say to me, 'I’m trying boss,' I would say to myself.

"But I’m certain it was that same insecurity that gave me the drive I have, that would make me run harder and train harder than everyone else.

"Ultimately that’s what gave me a career at the top level, because physically I was a machine and I took a lot of pride in that.

"Was the way I am a blessing or a curse for me? A bit of both I think. But you can only play the cards you’re dealt and try and make the best of them.

"I’m writing all this because I hope some young players might read it. You guys have so much confidence these days!

"I wish I could nick some of it and take it back in time, but confidence without application and having that fire in your belly to improve everyday won’t get you far.

"I see less young players doing extras, working on their craft, doing extra running after training. Trust me, you won’t have a career if you neglect this aspect.

"Try and find the sweetspot. That’s why I love guys like Bukayo Saka. He’s got that swagger, but you only need to listen to him in a post-match interview to see he’s never lost his humility.

"Find the sweetspot. Hopefully the above has some value to someone out there. I didn’t want to write the generic retirement, 'Thanks for everything,’ post as it seemed like a missed opportunity.

"Although of course I am very grateful to my friends, family, coaches, managers and of course the fans who have been with me on my journey. I’m looking forward to seeing what life has in store for me next."

Jenkinson came through the youth ranks at Charlton before joining Arsenal in 2011.

The right-back went on to make 70 appearances for the Gunners, mostly under Wenger, lifting the FA Cup in his third season at the club.

5 Jenkinson took part in Bromley's title celebrations having made five League Two outings last term Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

He scored once for his boyhood club in a 2-0 win at Norwich on the final day of the 2013/14 Premier League campaign.

After loan spells with West Ham and Birmingham, Jenkinson went on to sign for Nottingham Forest in 2019 on a permanent deal.

Despite the disappointment of his Arsenal exit, Jenkinson admitted he was happy to go back to supporting the Gunners.

"It was difficult. I was so sad that it had come to an end. I needed a bit of time to get over the fact that I wasn’t a player anymore," he told The Athletic in 2023.

"I think I just needed a little bit of time to become a fan again."

Jenkinson has also appeared on talkSPORT since leaving Arsenal, revealing the best Gunners team he ever played with and likening current Gunners boss Mikel Arteta to club legend Thierry Henry.

Following his time at Forest, Jenkinson headed to Australia, where he won the A-League title with Melbourne City, before returning to England with Bromley two years ago.

He also turned out for Welling United and Eastbourne Borough - on loan from Charlton - as well as another Australian sidein Newcastle Jets.

Sports.title: Aston Villa agree £34.2million deal to sign new goalkeeper amid Emiliano Martinez transfer offer
Sports.content:
Aston Villa have agreed a deal to sign goalkeeper Zion Suzuki from Parma, talkSPORT understands.

Suzuki's move to the Midlands to potentially replace Emiliano Martinez between the sticks is worth a total package of £34.2million.

3 Villa have agreed to sign Suzuki from Parma amid interest in Martinez Credit: Getty

Villa will fork out an initial £30m, with £4.2m to be paid in potential add-ons.

Japan international Suzuki will sign a five-year contract at Villa Park after agreeing on personal terms.

talkSPORT exclusively revealed on Saturday that talks had advanced between Aston Villa and Italian side Parma after a proposed transfer to Paris Saint-Germain collapsed.

Unai Emery's push to sign Suzuki has come after Juventus revived their interest in Martinez.

Will Suzuki replace Martinez at Villa?

Juventus have made an £8.5m package offer to sign Martinez from Aston Villa this summer, continuing their summer-long pursuit.

The Serie A giants were interested in signing the Argentinian goalkeeper before the World Cup began.

Martinez had told Villa that he wanted to leave and join Juve in June, but director of football Damian Vidagany shut that down.

They have now come back in for their man though, making a fresh bid split into a £6m fixed fee plus £2.5m in add-ons.

It's understood that Villa want the full £8.5m up front, while Martinez is likely to have to take a wage cut.

However, there is optimism that a deal can be struck for the 33-year-old to make the move to Italy - despite caution from the Old Lady regarding Martinez's broken finger.

3 Martinez has spent six years at Aston Villa, but could now be on the move to Juve Credit: Getty

And the imminent arrival of Suzuki could well make a departure more likely for the two-time Best FIFA Men's goalkeeper.

Suzuki's career so far

Suzuki is set to leave Parma after spending the last two years with the club, playing 57 times in Serie A.

His impressive performances have attracted interest from European giants for some time, with Manchester United looking at signing him as a replacement for Andre Onana last summer.

That switch didn't happen though, and the Japanese shot-stopper remained in Italy for another year.

Since then, he has starred for his nation at the World Cup, starting all four of Japan's games in North America.

Suzuki, who was born in the USA but grew up in Japan, began his professional career with J1 League club Urawa Red Diamonds.

3 Suzuki kept six clean sheets in 22 appearances for Parma last season Credit: Getty

He spent a season on loan at Sint-Truiden in 2023 and eventually joined them permanently a year later - but just a few months after that, Parma swooped in to sign him for a reported £8.5m.

Now, the 6'3" keeper is on his way to England and the Premier League, having played 59 games in Italy and 28 matches for Japan.

Sports.title: Newcastle win £30million race for World Cup star – and now eye up transfer hijack
Sports.content:
Newcastle win £30million race for World Cup star – and now eye up transfer hijack

Newcastle are set to make Benfica right-back Amar Dedic their sixth signing of the summer, talkSPORT understands.

The 23-year-old Bosnia and Herzegovina international will undergo a medical with the Magpies on Sunday.



3 Dedic has been identified by Newcastle to be Kieran Trippier's replacement Credit: Getty

It is believed that the deal is worth £30million, with Newcastle beating several clubs – including from the Premier League – to Dedic's signature.

The former Red Bull Salzburg player, who can operate in both full-back positions, has made 46 appearances for Benfica since joining the Portuguese giants last summer.

He also played three games at the 2026 World Cup as Bosnia reached the knockout stage for the first time.



Dedic is poised to become Newcastle's first defensive acquisition of the transfer window – one which has seen the Magpies have to rebuild generally amid the departures of Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes - and right-back Kieran Trippier.

With head coach Eddie Howe also stepping down to be replaced by Matthias Jaissle, it's a summer of big change at St James' Park.



Dedic might not be Newcastle's final signing between now and deadline day on August 31, however.

Former Fulham and Tottenham defensive midfielder Joao Palhinha, now at Bayern Munich, could make a return to the Premier League – with Newcastle potentially getting revenge on Aston Villa after they hijacked the Magpies' move for Johan Manzambi.



What has been said about the Joao Palhinha transfer saga?

"And Joao Palhinha could still be one to watch," talkSPORT's Ben Jacobs explained on the Sunday Edition with Shaun Custis and Henry Winter.

"So, we knew from last week that Palhinha would have liked to go to Aston Villa.

"Villa were offering a loan with a buy option, Bayern said permanent transfer only.

3 Palhinha was a key player on loan at Spurs last term Credit: Getty



"So, if Villa want to come back on that one and revive their interest, they need to make sure it's a permanent transfer – and if they did that, then Palhinha likes Villa.

"But at the moment, they haven't done that and Newcastle are prepared to make a permanent offer for Palhinha.

"And he would like to stay within the Premier League even though he has interest from Benfica as well.

"So, we might see another experienced and Premier League-ready midfielder arrive at St James' Park between now and the end of the window.



"In fact, we will – it's just a case of whether it's going to be Palhinha or another name."

Portugal international Palhinha joined Bayern from Fulham in 2024, but returned to the Premier League with Spurs on loan last season, scoring five goals in 33 appearances.

3 Palhinha featured in 33 Premier League matches last season - starting on 23 occasions

Newcastle conclude their pre-season with a friendly against Strasbourg on Sunday – the second of a double-header at St James' Park which began with a 2-1 loss to Bayer Leverkusen on Saturday.



The Magpies kick off the 2026/27 campaign at home to Liverpool next Sunday (August 23).

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta sweating over new Premier League rule which could hinder set-piece kings
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta sweating over new Premier League rule which could hinder set-piece kings

Mikel Arteta has admitted Arsenal will need to adopt a new approach after the Premier League banned towels from being used to dry balls.

The Gunners were the Premier League's set-piece specialists last season en route to lifting their first top-flight title in 22 years.



4 Arsenal were the Premier League's set-piece kings last season Credit: Getty

The north London giants scored 25 set-piece goals, excluding penalties - the most in the division.

However, they will be forced into a change in approach owing to the latest change in the rules.

Towels were permitted to be used in Premier League matches last season, provided both teams agreed to do so.



The rule itself surfaced during Arsenal's eventual 2-1 win at Newcastle back in September.

Riccardo Calafiori sought to use a towel to dry the ball before launching a missile into the box, but was denied the opportunity to do so by referee Jarred Gillett.



Now, towels have been banned entirely, meaning teams can't dry a ball before a throw-in is taken.

What has Mikel Arteta said about the towel rule change?

Speaking ahead of Sunday's Community Shield clash with Manchester City, Arteta said of the upcoming rule change: "Not being able to use the towels is already a big one."



The Spaniard then joked that his players could now wear hats in order to dry their hands before taking a throw.

He quipped: "Let’s see what we do. Maybe we will play with hats on!"

There will not only be a new towel ruling coming into play this season, but also a 'five second' restart rule to combat time-wasting.

4 Declan Rice will not be able to use a towel to dry balls for throw-ins this season Credit: Getty

That is in addition to a crackdown on goalkeeper tactical timeouts, as well as a new substitution law.



Arteta was asked which of the new rules will have the biggest impact on the game.

To which he said: "We have had the Premier League and the referees there with us to explain and go through everything.

“In pre-season we had the opportunity to see and experience some of them.

“We will have to see when the season starts and how this unfolds and what is more doable and what is less doable and what we need to adapt.



“We know that everybody is paying so much to the details, all the restarts and the countdowns, that will bring something else, a different dynamic, different momentum.

4 Arteta is looking to guide Arsenal to back-to-back Premier League titles for the first time Credit: Getty

"So I am very curious to see. They are really good rules because what we are doing is trying to promote more game time and the fluidity of the games which is better and hopefully that will work.”

What did Sean Dyche say about towels being used?

The new towel ruling comes months after former Nottingham Forest boss and talkSPORT regular Sean Dyche called for them to be banned entirely following a meeting with Brentford back in January.



Dyche was incensed by the amount of time it took for Bees full-back Michael Kayode to dry the ball before taking a throw-in.

"They have towels on the sidelines. I can't work that out," Dyche said following Forest's 2-0 win at Brentford.

"Nothing against Brentford. It's the rules. How can a home team be allowed to decide if they have towels on the sidelines or not?"

The EFL implemented a complete towel ban ahead of the 2023/24 season, which Dyche felt should have also impacted the Premier League.



4 Dyche complained about the use of towels in the Premier League last season Credit: Getty

"Why not in the Premier League, just go, no towels, just get on with the game?

"It just adds in another layer of things for us to talk about and for us to worry about.

"Just say no towels. Dead easy, isn't it? It's not rocket science. Why make it more complicated? It's unfathomable to me."

Sports.title: Newcastle and Everton joined by Premier League rival in race to sign Chelsea striker Liam Delap
Sports.content:
Newcastle and Everton joined by Premier League rival in race to sign Chelsea striker Liam Delap

Nottingham Forest have joined the race to sign Liam Delap with the player keen to stay in the Premier League, talkSPORT understands.

The Chelsea striker has been told he can leave Stamford Bridge this summer, as the club look to trim down their huge first-team squad.



4 Liam Delap has been part of Chelsea's pre-season tour of Australia and Asia this summer, despite ongoing speculation over his future Credit: Getty

After his £30million arrival from Ipswich last summer, Delap endured a nightmare debut season in west London.

The 23-year-old struck just once in the Premier League and twice overall in an injury-hit campaign.

Chelsea now appear keen to cash in on him before the transfer window's September 1st deadline, especially following the arrival of Danny Welbeck from Brighton.



Who has been linked with Liam Delap?

Having drawn Premier League interest from several Premier League clubs, Delap has now emerged as a target for Italian side Como.

talkSPORT understands Chelsea are demanding £40m for Delap, which would represent a £10m profit for the west Londoners.



However, Como might struggle to strike up a deal for the Englishman, who wants to stay in the Premier League.

That's despite a move to Italy offering Delap the chance to play Champions League football.



The Serie A side are managed by former Blues star Cesc Fabregas, and sealed qualification for Europe's premier competition with a fourth-placed finish in Serie A last term.

Chelsea, meanwhile, won't be playing in Europe altogether after finishing a disappointing 10th in the 2025/26 Premier League season.

Como have already signed one player from the Blues this summer having snapped up defender Trevoh Chalobah earlier this month.

4 Cesc Fabregas has earned a growing reputation since taking charge of Como in 2024 Credit: Getty



4 Chelsea are looking to make a profit on Delap, despite a tough debut season in west London Credit: Getty

Back to the drawing board

With Delap appearing unwilling to leave English football, this considerably narrows down where he could go next.

While Newcastle and Everton have both been credited with interest, this hasn't progressed into any concrete offers.

And talkSPORT's Ben Jacobs has declared that Delap is also on Forest's radar ahead of a potential deal.



With Taiwo Awoniyi poised to join top-flight newcomers Coventry, Forest could well be in the market for a centre-forward late in the transfer window.

In any case, it remains likely that Delap's future lies away from Stamford Bridge, with Chelsea keen to reduce their attacking options this summer.

The arrival of Danny Welbeck from Brighton bolstered the Blues forward line, which also boasts 15-goal striker Joao Pedro from last season.

4 Delap became a hot property in the 2025/26 campaign with Ipswich Credit: Getty



As well as Welbeck, the Blues have signed Emmanuel Emegha from Strasbourg – though the Netherlands international could already be on his way out of Stamford Bridge, albeit not permanently.

With new boss Xabi Alonso clear on who he wants to keep, Chelsea are also looking to sell Nicolas Jackson, who is linked with Aston Villa.

As for Delap, he is looking for a move that will see him get back to the form that made Chelsea shell out £30m to sign him from Ipswich.

He scored 12 goals in 2024/25 - the Tractor Boys' first campaign back in the top flight - so he has shown he can cut it at this level and that he could be a very handy addition for another club.



Delap must also have his international career in mind, having represented England up to under-21 level.

The Manchester City youth product has yet to be called up to the Three Lions senior squad, however.

The frontman is also eligible to play for the Republic of Ireland through his ancestry, with his father - Premier League cult hero Rory Delap - earning 11 caps for the country.

Sports.title: Bamba Dieng told to snub Middlesbrough transfer and join Premier League club instead
Sports.content:
Bamba Dieng told to snub Middlesbrough transfer and join Premier League club instead

Bamba Dieng should snub a move to Middlesbrough and join Hull City instead.

That's the view of European football expert Andy Brassell, who has has commented on reports that the two clubs are in a race to secure the forward's services.

3 Hull City are Brassell's favourites to sign Senegal international Bamba Credit: Getty

The Tigers defeated Boro in the Championship play-off final last term to earn promotion to the top-flight for the upcoming campaign.

Dieng is currently a free agent after departing Lorient at the end of last season, drawing significant interest from clubs across France, Spain, and Turkey.

The Senegal international is proving to be hot property after netting 16 goals in 26 appearances, a run that earned him a place in Senegal's World Cup squad.

The 26-year-old performed a dramatic U-turn earlier in the summer after appearing set to join newly promoted Super Lig side Amedspor.

Now, Brassell has tipped the frontman to seal a move to newly promoted Premier League outfit Hull.

What has Brassell said about Dieng?

He said: "It's got to be the Tigers, right? I think the chance to show that you could do it in the Premier League, and Bamba Dieng actually had a really decent season last year.

"Go back a couple of years and his reputation was on the floor.

"He’s not playing the way that he would have wanted to.

"But he's brought his career back to life in the last year and was really impressive."

Dieng is no stranger to chaotic transfer deadline-day drama throughout his career.

3 Dieng played against England at the 2022 Qatar World Cup Credit: Getty

In 2022, the striker was on the verge of joining Leeds United before Nice hijacked the deal at the eleventh hour.

After flying to France, the transfer collapsed amidst medical and contractual complications, leaving the player in the awkward position of returning to Marseille.

The situation damaged his relationship with the hierarchy at the French club, which led to reduced game time and a stagnation in his development.

Additionally, he suffered multiple injuries including ankle and groin issues further interrupted his momentum.

He eventually made the move to Lorient in 2023, yet initially struggled to secure a permanent role in the team.

However, he bounced back with strong scoring spells for the club and was able to re-establish his profile as a clinical forward.

3 Pagis' partnership with Dieng seen Lorient finish tenth Credit: AFP

What do Hull City need?

Brassell commented on his most recent season, and said: "He showed his ability to dovetail with other quality players as well. He's got pace. He's strong. He's inventive.

"We've seen him link up with the likes of Pablo Pagis, who moved to Paris FC this summer, it's a good effect. So we've always known that there's a player there.

"He made some unusual career choices after leaving Marseille, but he's now at a place where he's coming off a strong campaign, he's shown how much he's still got to give as well.

"There's definitely a leap he can make, and It's very impressive - He's got his career back."

To survive in the top-flight, Hull City will need to maintain tactical flexibility and rely on the sharp counter-attacking football that served them so well in the Championship under Sergej Jakirović.

Despite the club boasting Oli McBurnie up front, additional attacking reinforcements will be essential to ensure adequate depth for their Premier League return.

Sports.title: West Ham smash EFL record to sign Arne Engels from Celtic
Sports.content:
West Ham have confirmed the £22million signing of Arne Engels ahead of their first Championship game of the season.

The Hammers get their domestic campaign underway on Sunday when they face fellow relegated side Burnley at Turf Moor.

3 Engels has made the move to the London Stadium on an initial five-year deal Credit: Getty

And West Ham signalled their intentions to make an immediate return to the Premier League as they broke the EFL record to lure Engels to the London Stadium.

The £22m deal eclipses the previous Championship record which was set by Ipswich last summer.

Ipswich splashed out £17.5m to snap up Norway forward Sindre Walle Egeli from Danish outlet FC Nordsjaelland.

Despite fan excitement over the arrival of Engels, the four-cap Belgium will not be involved in the clash against the Clarets.

Having not been signed in time to be registered, his debut will likely come against Charlton next weekend.

Engels will wear the No.7 shirt in east London, with the number vacant following the departure of Crysensio Sumemrville.

What has Arne Engels said about joining West Ham?

And he has failed to hide his delight at penning a five-year deal at the London Stadium, with his deal containing the option of a further 12 months.

He told West Ham's website: "It feels amazing to be here, so I'm delighted and I can't wait to get started.

"It's a really nice project to come into and try to to go back to the Premier League. That's the big goal.

"I think that's everybody's goal and it's just up to me to hopefully help the team with it and together with the supporters to get some wins.

3 Engels completed his EFL-record move south of the border on Saturday night Credit: Getty

"Hopefully, we'll see that it's going to be a good year then and I'm looking forward to the next ones.

"I'm just looking forward to meeting all the fans at London Stadium.

"I’m looking forward to this challenging season, but hopefully we can make it a really good one, so let's go for it!"

West Ham's summer business

West Ham's relegation meant the Hammers were initially forced into high-profile sales to help balance the books.

Mateus Fernandes and Summerville both left for Tottenham and Al Hilal respectively in £100m and £68m moves.

Freddie Potts meanwhile was sold for £10m, with Callum Wilson, Adama Traore and Lukasz Fabianski also departing the club.

3 Fernandes was one of two big-money sales at the London Stadium this summer Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

A boost for West Ham, though, was that they were able to retain the services of captain Jarrod Bowen.

And West Ham have since started to bolster the squad having brought in defender Joel Veltman following his release from Brighton.

Manor Solomon has also signed for the Hammers, joining from London rivals Spurs.

Sports.title: Amy Hunt and Team GB stars caught up in armed police drama after winning gold at the European Championships as man in his thirties is arrested
Sports.content:
Amy Hunt and her gold medal-winning relay team-mates were caught up in a huge security operation that brought travel chaos to the European Championships in Birmingham on Saturday night.

Armed police arrived in significant numbers at the Alexander Stadium after a man in his thirties was spotted behaving suspiciously at around 8.15pm. He was later arrested on suspicion of fraud.

The episode caused the cancellation of six medal ceremonies inside the venue, with major disruptions erupting outside. Buses for spectators and hundreds of athletes and coaches, including the one carrying Hunt and the rest of the victorious 4x100m quartet, were delayed by up to two hours.

It is understood that police conducted searches on buses that were due to ferry competitors, staff and fans back to the city centre. As of Sunday morning, the individual arrested by West Midlands Police was still in custody.

Amy Hunt and her Team GB team-mates were held up during an armed police operation

Athletes and spectators faced travel chaos in Birmingham following Saturday night's action

A statement from championship organisers read: ‘Championship transport was suspended until the necessary security measures had been carried out whilst West Midlands Police arrested a man in his thirties on suspicion of fraud. The safety and wellbeing of our spectators, athletes, workforce and the wider Championships’ family will always be our first priority.

‘We recognise that the delays presented challenges for those affected and would like to thank everyone for their patience, understanding and cooperation throughout the evening. Further information will be issued on Sunday relating to the evening’s postponed medal ceremonies.’

West Midlands Police said: ‘A man was arrested following concerns of suspicious activity at the European Athletics Championship last night.

‘At around 8.15pm, concerns were raised after a man was found in an area of Alexander Stadium with the wrong accreditation.

‘As a precaution, security measures were put in place and transport for the Championship staff and athletes were suspended. This then led to delays to transport from the stadium for the wider public.

‘A man in his 30s was arrested on suspicion of fraud and remains in custody for questioning.

‘We understand the concern this may have caused and can confirm there was no immediate risk to the public.

‘As always, our priority is the safety of the public and we want to thank everyone for the patience.’

Hunt will return to the stadium in Sunday in pursuit of a record-breaking fourth gold medal in the 4x100m mixed relay.

Sports.title: Why a crackdown on set-pieces could leave Arsenal exposed as Mikel Arteta reveals Gunners are looking to adapt to new rules
Sports.content:
Why a crackdown on set-pieces could leave Arsenal exposed as Mikel Arteta reveals Gunners are looking to adapt to new rules

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Mikel Arteta hinted that Arsenal may have to adapt their set-piece routines after an influx of new rules ahead of the upcoming season.

The 2026-27 campaign will feature an unprecedented number of new laws, mostly designed to make the game flow quicker.

These changes will be deployed right through English football this weekend, including Arsenal’s Community Shield match against Manchester City on Sunday.

The laws include countdowns for goal-kicks and throw-ins, time-limited substitutions and a crackdown on holding during set-pieces.

The Gunners have courted attention previously for their physical set-plays and it remains to be seen how they will adapt to stay within the rules.

On the changes, Arteta said: ‘We have had the Premier League and the referees there with us to explain and go through everything.

Mikel Arteta has hinted Arsenal may have to adapt their approach to set pieces with new rules having been introduced ahead of the new season

Arteta's side attracted attention for their physical set-plays and it remains to be seen how they will adapt to stay within the rules

‘In pre-season we had the opportunity to see and experience some of them. We will have to see when the season starts and how this unfolds and what is more doable and what is less doable and what we need to adapt.

‘There are a few (which will have a big impact). Not being able to use the towels is already a big one in the Premier League. Let’s see what we do. Maybe we will play with hats on!

‘Something else will come up for sure. We know that everybody is paying so much to the details, all the restarts and the countdowns, that will bring someone else, a different dynamic, different momentum.

‘So I am very curious to see. They are really good rules because what we are doing is trying to promote more game time and the fluidity of the games which is better and hopefully that will work.’

Meanwhile, Arteta said he will have to elevate his level to keep up with the influx of new managers across the Premier League’s Big Six clubs.

The managerial landscape has changed significantly, with Enzo Maresca replacing Pep Guardiola at Man City, while Andoni Iraola has taken over from Arne Slot at Liverpool.

Chelsea have also appointed a new manager in Xabi Alonso, who replaced Maresca, and Michael Carrick was handed the permanent job at Manchester United in May.

Tottenham have also turned to Roberto De Zerbi, who took charge at the end of the 2025–26 season.

Arteta added: ‘We will have a lot of challengers looking at the squads, at the managers and at the clubs they are, but we know that.

‘We need to focus on ourselves and making sure that we maximise every resource we have to give ourselves the best chance. Then day by day it is going to be a long, long run.

‘Well, with a few managers as well and some new ones coming into the league that are exceptional. We know this league is full of incredible managers. It is so challenging every week to prepare games against them. That will elevate our level and my level for sure and we will try to be better.’

Juventus are hopeful of signing Emiliano Martinez from Aston Villa despite doubts over a finger injury.

The Serie A club are prepared to make an initial offer of about £6million for Martinez, plus performance-related bonuses

Sports.title: West Ham's fresh start: The revamped transfer operation and what's behind it, two new faces leading promotion charge and a return to the 'Academy of Football'
Sports.content:
West Ham's fresh start: The revamped transfer operation and what's behind it, two new faces leading promotion charge and a return to the 'Academy of Football'

Unlock more from inside the West Ham camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

An hour or so before West Ham got their season underway, a few of the journalists inside the London Stadium started to place bets.

David Sullivan, the unpopular former co-chair, was expected to be there against everyone’s advice, so how long would it take for the home fans to send the first message his way? Thirty seconds? Five minutes? Whenever the first Portsmouth goal went in, surely?

This was, after all, a fanbase that has tirelessly protested against the running of their once great club. Boycotts, banners, black balloons and yet, despite all their warnings, they now head to Burnley on Sunday to begin their first season in the Championship in 14 years. Even after Sullivan resigned amid allegations of sexual misconduct, which he denies, here he still was casting his shadow.

In the end, all predictions passed without incident, even after the Hammers went behind. Sixty-three minutes needed to tick by before the crowd of more than 53,000, a quite ludicrous record number for the first round of the League Cup, rose in unison amid demands to ‘Stand up, if you hate the board’. Sullivan is no longer on it, of course, but you got the drift.

They were much more eager to direct their anger at a first-half hydration break set to dance music but, more than anything, it was as though they were not going to allow an unwanted visitor to ruin their hopes of a new dawn.

Sullivan might have been there in person, and still own more of the club for now than anyone else, but his hands are no longer on the steering wheel, nor is it the ink from his pen drying on the cheques.

West Ham still, incredibly, have Jarrod Bowen, who committed his future to the club despite their relegation to the Championship

David Sullivan (left), the unpopular co-chairman, attended the first game of the season against everyone else's best advice

He can watch, as he did last Saturday, and confide in those around him that the team needs more pace, another striker and a creative midfielder, but he’s not in a position anymore to do much about it, even if his son is still angling to get some young lads on trial. Karren Brady isn’t there anymore either. ‘No more BS’ was the message on the red cards fans brandished last season, in a nod to Brady and Sullivan. They go into the season having got their wish.

And they still, incredibly, have Jarrod Bowen. Over the past three Premier League seasons, only Erling Haaland, Mo Salah, Ollie Watkins, Cole Palmer and Bruno Fernandes scored more goals than Bowen. Now, he’s playing in the Championship. Good luck, everyone.

New signing Manor Solomon, signed for £10million from Tottenham, said Bowen’s decision to stay helped convince him to make the move to east London.

‘I thought, like everyone else, that Jarrod would leave this summer and go to the Premier League, even to one of the top teams, but he decided to stay,’ said Solomon. ‘It was one of the key reasons why I decided to sign for West Ham.’

Club insiders talk of a fresh start and, at long last, finding a sense of normality. Not many football clubs are all that normal deep down but few have been less able to claim it in recent years than West Ham. Nils Koppen, the new head of recruitment, has not been at the club long but is already trying to put data-led systems in place to ensure smooth running of the transfer operation.

It’s one that’s bagged Brighton full back Joel Veltman on a free transfer, Solomon from Tottenham, and is on the verge of signing £22million Celtic midfielder Arne Engels.

‘Patient is a good word but it is, more than anything, about trying to make it right,’ explained boss Nuno Espirito Santo. ‘All the deals we want to make, the player has to come with a purpose, with a clear mindset of what we expect. We don’t have too much time but the priority is to make it right.’

It’s not always been that way.

New signing Manor Solomon, who joined for £10million from Tottenham, said Bowen’s decision to stay helped convince him to make the move to east London

Club insiders talk of a fresh start and finding a sense of normality. Not many football clubs are all that normal deep down but few have been less able to claim it recently than West Ham

‘Anyone who can put those processes in place will revolutionise West Ham,’ one insider told Daily Mail Sport.

This is a club that’s been so remarkably short of them. Koppen is the fourth recruitment boss in just 18 months after Tim Steidten, Kyle Macaulay and Max Hahn, so is it any wonder that the Hammers are still having to right the many, many wrongs of previous transfer windows.

Mateus Fernandes and Crysencio Summerville have been sold for the best part of £150million but there’s other deadwood that needs shifting. Nuno wants rid of Niclas Fullkrug and Jean-Clair Todibo. Brentford have enquired about full back El Hadji Malick Diouf, who only signed last summer for £20million, while Aston Villa have held talks over Aaron Wan-Bissaka.

Few signings encapsulate West Ham’s ridiculous running over recent years like that of Todibo, originally loaned in from Nice by Steidten with an obligation to buy should they stay up. By the time that came around, Steidten was gone and so was manager Julen Lopetegui.

Todibo clashed with his replacement Graham Potter, was dropped for bad timekeeping, then refused to play in West Ham’s survival showdown against Leeds on the final day of last season under Nuno, having told him he would not play for him again. The Frenchman did not attend West Ham's media day for this season so has a generic close-up picture of his face on the official website unlike the rest of the squad, who all posed in the new home kit. Wan-Bissaka and Fullkrug also missed it.

West Ham remain in talks with Arsenal over a move for winger Reiss Nelson and want Chelsea centre back Axel Disasi, who impressed hugely on loan last season. The Hammers are after Ireland striker Troy Parrott and are also keeping an eye on former Leicester front man Jamie Vardy as a potential back-up. How fun might that be? Vardy is nearly 40 but that didn’t stop Teddy Sheringham from firing West Ham to promotion all those years ago.

The ongoing, messy and complex boardroom struggles rumble on, too, with Czech billionaire and West Ham stakeholder Daniel Kretinsky wrestling it out with former Newcastle co-owner Amanda Staveley over the shares of David Gold’s family. Staveley has an eye on Sullivan’s, too.

Few signings encapsulate West Ham’s ridiculous running over recent years like that of Jean-Clair Todibo

Mohamadou Kante has the physicality that just might suit the rough and tumble of the Championship

Some behind the scenes are excited by the prospect of Staveley’s involvement, with one source describing her as ‘proper switched on’, yet it was Kretinsky whose pitch persuaded Bowen to stay and lead the promotion challenge.

West Ham might just have a few budding youngsters to help him, too. It had become a bit of a running gag that West Ham called themselves the ‘Academy of Football’ yet failed to hand a single full Premier League debut to a graduate of their youth system in five years from February 2020.

There won't be one this season for obvious reasons, and one of their most recent additions to the ‘Wall of Graduates’ at their Chadwell Heath base Freddie Potts, son of club legend Steve, has just joined Club Bruges on a permanent deal. Hammers never like to see one of their own depart, especially one with that much claret and blue running through his veins.

The emergence of Lewis Orford and Mohamadou Kante, though, provides two reasons why the club felt it was worth banking the £10million for Potts.

Orford impressed Nuno during pre-season and has been referred to behind the scenes as having a touch of Michael Carrick about him. He has been at the club since he was five. His parents, grandfather and girlfriend sat in the stands to watch him control the midfield against Portsmouth. Kante has the physicality that just might suit the rough and tumble of the Championship.

And so, despite all the upheaval and uncertainty, there was a genuine feeling around the London Stadium last Saturday that this is a club ready to embrace their fresh start.

Sports.title: Former Arsenal star Carl Jenkinson opens up on career-long 'insecurity' in emotional statement as he announces retirement from football aged 34
Sports.content:
Former Arsenal and England defender Carl Jenkinson has revealed he struggled with 'insecurity' his whole career as he announced his retirement.

The 34-year-old brought the curtain down on his playing days on Sunday in an emotional statement in which he admitted to his struggles and revealed advice from Arsene Wenger that he struggled to take on board.

Jenkinson, who was capped once by England in November 2012, played for the likes of Charlton, Arsenal and West Ham in his career, before finishing up with Bromley as part of the side that won League Two last season.

Now, though, he has taken the time to reflect, revealing that his professional days have come to an end.

'Thank you to everyone who played a part in my journey, from my Charlton days as a kid through to my last time playing football at Bromley,' the statement began. 'From the age of 8 football has been my life, it's given me a lot, and I have also given it a lot back. In fact I've given it everything.

'It's for that reason that I can write this looking back over my career with no regrets. Do I wish certain things went better? Without a doubt. A lot of things. I once scored an own goal from 30 yards out. I certainly wouldn't mind deleting that from history. But were these bad or difficult moments ever because of a lack of effort? No. Like I said, I gave football everything. Everyday.

Former Arsenal defender Carl Jenkinson has opened up on his career struggles as he revealed his retirement from football

'And I guess I'm writing this because I can see that's getting lost a bit these days. I don't know if it's social media painting a certain picture of what a footballer looks like, but I want to be clear, behind the scenes these top players train like their life depends on it. Alexis Sanchez, wow. Every training session he trained like it was his last. The ones that don't, they fall by the way side eventually. Even when they're really, really good. I've seen it happen to too many young pros and scholars, trying to make a name in the game.

'Apply yourself everyday, listen to your coaches and learn from the players who have already been where you want to get to. Because if you don't make it, and it's because you got carried away with yourself, it'll be a heavy burden to carry later in life.

'I suffered a lot with confidence throughout my career, which I found strange because my Dad always backs himself to the hilt. I saw loads of people, to try and unlock something within me and find that inner belief. "Take the chains off" Arsene Wenger would say to me. "I'm trying boss", I would say to myself. But I'm certain it was that same insecurity that gave me the drive I have, that would make me run harder and train harder than everyone else.

'Ultimately that's what gave me a career at the top level, because physically I was a machine and I took a lot of pride in that. Was the way I am a blessing or a curse for me? A bit of both I think. But you can only play the cards you're dealt and try and make the best of them.'

Jenkinson joined Arsenal for what was thought to have been around £1million in 2012 as a youngster with high hopes.

He never really hit the heights many had expected, but still enjoyed a long career in the game.

It's unclear if he will stay in football post-retirement, but took the opportunity to pass on some wisdom to younger players in his post.

'I'm writing all this because I hope some young players might read it,' he continued. 'You guys have so much confidence these days! I wish I could nick some of it and take it back in time, but confidence without application and having that fire in your belly to improve everyday won't get you far.

Jenkinson, now 34, offered advice for young players after finishing up with Bromley

'I see less young players doing extras, working on their craft, doing extra running after training. Trust me, you won't have a career if you neglect this aspect.

'Try and find the sweetspot. That's why I love guys like Bukayo Saka. He's got that swagger, but you only need to listen to him in a post match interview to see he's never lost his humility. Find the sweetspot.

'Hopefully the above has some value to someone out there. I didn't want to write the generic retirement 'thanks for everything' post as it seemed like a missed opportunity. Although of course I am very grateful to my friends, family, coaches, managers and of course the fans who have been with me on my journey. I'm looking forward to seeing what life has in store for me next.

'Cheers, Jenko.'

Sports.title: Australia have been papering over the cracks and their embarrassing defeat by Bangladesh leaves them exposed - but after England's failed attempt to resurrect Bazball, now both teams are in a race to be ready for next summer's Ashes
Sports.content:
One of the challenges in the immediate aftermath of Bangladesh's stunning nine-wicket win in the first Test against Australia at Darwin was to arrange emotions in a socially acceptable sequence.

The general consensus was something like this: Bangladesh brilliant, Australia abject, England embarrassed, though some Down Under preferred reversing that order. Coping mechanisms, eh? We've all been there. And yet Australia really do have plenty to cope with right now.

It's right and proper that we salute the Bangladeshi heroes: Hasan Mahmud's first-innings six-for, a century for Tanzid Hasan and 84 for captain Nazmul Hossain Shanto, and a second-innings five-for from Mehidy Hasan. This was the greatest result in their history, against a team who had deigned to play them only twice in the previous 20 years.

But Australia will be doing themselves no favours if they don't use this result as a chance to reset their team in time for the 2027 Ashes. Clearly, it's not just England who have questions to answer with less than a year to go before the resumption of Test cricket's longest-running narrative.

The recent Ashes, as has been pointed out on a regular basis these past few days, papered over cracks wider than the one hit by Mitchell Starc to bowl James Vince at the WACA in 2017-18.

Against England, only Travis Head, Steve Smith and Alex Carey averaged more than 29, allowing Marnus Labuschagne (28), Cameron Green (24) and Jake Weatherald (22) to huddle together under the radar.

Australia have been exposed and need to reset their team ahead of the next Ashes in 2027

England, now under Joe Root, have wasted eight months post-Ashes - shouldn't allow themselves too much schadenfreude

And while Green – to the quiet delight of England fans – has probably cemented his place with his second-innings hundred, Labuschagne's match double of one (in 35 minutes) and 31 leaves him without a Test hundred in 42 innings, in which time he has averaged 25. Weatherald, meanwhile, has not passed 34 in nine innings since England fed his cut shot at the Gabba.

The bowling is another matter. English observers may feel, only half-jokingly, that Bangladesh got off lightly not having to face either Scott Boland or Michael Neser, who hoovered up 35 wickets between them during the Ashes at a rate of one every 44 balls.

On the other hand, Boland will be 38 by the time Australia land at Heathrow next summer, and Neser 37, embodying the issues faced by an ageing attack: Nathan Lyon will be 39, Mitchell Starc 37, Josh Hazlewood 36 and Pat Cummins 34.

We've been here before, of course: the Dad's Army jibes were bandied about all too easily before England landed in Perth in November, and look how that ended up. But Australia now face a tough decision. Do they give all their old-timers one last chance to win a series in England, or do they use the next few months to refresh and renew?

You suspect their hand will be forced, because their schedule is punishing: after the second Test against Bangladesh in Mackay, they face three in South Africa in October, then four at home to New Zealand in December and January, followed immediately by five in India, and the 150th pink-ball game against England at the MCG.

If Australia don't replenish their ranks, they may have no one left by the time they arrive to defend the urn.

And that is where England shouldn't allow themselves too much schadenfreude. After all, they have just wasted the eight months since the Ashes reaching the obvious conclusion that Brendon McCullum was no longer the right man to coach the Test team, and are about to take on Pakistan with a new-not-new captain in Joe Root and a coach, Marcus Trescothick, who is keeping the seat warm for Stephen Fleming.

Traditionally, Australia have reacted more swiftly to defeat than England, because their tolerance of failure is much lower, their expectation of excellence a given. Already, Ricky Ponting is making noises about the need for change.

You can be sure that, once the Australians have stopped pointing out why Bangladesh's win showed the Poms how it should have been done, they will steel themselves for a crazy 12 months. Can England say the same?

Sports.title: Revealed: World Cup final referee's plea to Lionel Messi to 'control' Argentina star Leandro Paredes before shameful full-time scenes - as new footage shows the moment he receives a medal from Donald Trump
Sports.content:
New footage has emerged of World Cup final referee begging Lionel Messi to 'control' Leandro Paredes before his violent outburst at full-time.

The game between Argentina and Spain descended into chaos after the final whistle last month, when Paredes lost his cool and launched an attack on Eric Garcia and Gavi after Spain were confirmed as champions.

Now, it has emerged that referee, Slavko Vincic of Slovenia, had pleaded with Argentina captain Messi earlier in the game to control one of football's biggest hot heads.

In footage shared from the successful referee cam, Vincic can be heard saying: 'Messi, control Paredes. I don't want to... he has yellow. Control please. Always, always.'

The midfielder, who was brought on at half-time and booked six minutes later, made it to full-time, but then lost his cool.

The 32-year-old grabbed defender Eric Garcia by the neck, pushed over Gavi and also appeared to throw punches after Argentina's defeat. He was also fortunate not to be sent off towards the end of normal time for a foul.

Footage has emerged of the World Cup final referee pleading with Lionel Messi to 'control' Leandro Paredes

FIFA has since launched disciplinary proceedings against Paredes for the unsavoury scenes – he faces three counts of assault as well as a charge of unsporting behaviour.

The ref cam, meawhile, also showed the moment Vincic received his medal from Donald Trump, when he was told he did a 'great job'.

Paredes has since returned to club action and played for Boca Juniors in their 2-2 draw at Newell's Old Boys two weeks ago in the Argentine Primera Division – Torneo Clausura.

And during that encounter, the 32-year-old was back producing some 'dark arts' with one particular flashpoint.

Trailing 2-1 to the hosts, Paredes started an on-pitch melee when he appeared to deliberately kick a ball at a stricken opponent on 68 minutes.

As the player, who had just been fouled, was returning to his feet and with his back turned, Paredes booted the ball at him.

The act saw angry players from Newell's Old Boys confront him before the referee brandished him a yellow card for his act.

Paredes had suggested he may quit international football in the aftermath of the World Cup final, telling ESPN: 'For many, it will be the time to decide if to continue. It was a great journey. Maintaining that level – getting the group to continue to function as it has - will be very difficult, and there are many factors to consider.

Paredes lost his cool after full-time against Spain as he clashed with Eric Garcia and Gavi

'Decisions must be taken calmly. I don't know yet if I'm ready to continue. It's a process that takes time to assimilate and mature.

'It will take time to digest what we've been through. The pain of losing the World Cup final will stay with us for a long time, because we came so close once again. I think we played in a World Cup where people saw themselves in us, and that's very rewarding. In that sense, I'm happy.'

His team-mate Enzo Fernandez, meanwhile received a frosty reception in his return to Chelsea duty.

There were perhaps expected boos when his name was read out before kick-off, with the World Cup runner-up starting on the bench.

But the atmosphere turned bizarre when he was introduced after an hour, with sections of the crowd booing him while others proudly sang his name. That continued when he had the ball in midfield, too, with disgruntled boos followed by encouraging chants.

Fernandez, who replaced Reece James and wore the captain's armband for the final 30 minutes, has been stuck in a complicated situation at Chelsea since he alerted the world in March that he dreams of playing for Real Madrid. Then-manager Liam Rosenior took umbrage and dropped him for two games in response.

The feeling this summer has been that his future lies away from Stamford Bridge, but his options are limited by few clubs having the financial capacity to meet Chelsea's valuation.

Manchester City were the front-runners, but Chelsea set suitors an unofficial deadline of 5pm Friday to make a sufficient offer as they want their squad fixed before their season opener against Fulham on August 24.

Although that deadline passed without an offer, it remains to be seen if a £120m bid between now and September 1 would test their resolve. What is for sure, though, is that Chelsea supporters do not know how to feel about it.

New FREE daily racing pullout launched in the Mirror with more tips, news and insight

For the first time ever, the national newspaper is offering racing readers a daily supplement with more racecards, tips, silks, news, insight and exclusive columns

View 3 Images The Daily Mirror is launching a new racing pullout (Image: John Walton/PA Wire)

The Mirror is launching a fantastic and free daily horse racing pullout for its band of loyal readers who love the sport of kings.

‌



It is the first time in its 123-year history that the paper has carried a racing supplement every weekday.

‌



From August 17, the Monday to Friday pullout will complement the Mirror’s award-winning Saturday section.

‌



It means that readers will get more tips, analysis, racecards, insight, exclusive columns and the latest news and gossip six days a week.

Our team is the best in the business – led by David Yates, aka Newsboy, one of the most prominent names in racing journalism, who will aim to help readers take on the bookies.

Sports.title: Harry Maguire backs Marcus Rashford for Man Utd stay - 'He is going to help us'
Sports.content:
Harry Maguire backs Marcus Rashford for Man Utd stay - 'He is going to help us'

Marcus Rashford made his first appearance for Manchester United since December 2024 in their pre-season friendly with AC Milan and Harry Maguire wants the attacker to stick around long-term

View 2 Images Harry Maguire wants Marcus Rashford to stay at Manchester United (Image: Andrzej Iwanczuk/NurPhoto)

Harry Maguire says that the Manchester United dressing room want Marcus Rashford to stay at the club following his return to the first team.

‌



Rashford had not made a competitive appearance for United since the fixture against Viktoria Plzen back in December 2024 prior to this weekend and was expected to join Barcelona permanently this summer after signing for them on loan last year. However, the Spanish giants declined to trigger an option to sign the England star permanently.

‌



With no other agreement in place for a transfer, Rashford has been left in limbo this summer with some suggesting he could now be reintegrated at Old Trafford by Michael Carrick.

‌



The attacker featured for 30 minutes as a substitute in Saturday's pre-season friendly defeat against AC Milan while wearing the No 9 shirt, further fuelling speculation that there could yet be another chapter in his Manchester United story.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

And Maguire made it clear that he and his team-mates hope the United academy graduate will still be a red when the transfer window closes. “He can improve us for sure,” the 33-year-old told The Athletic. “I think you have seen when he came on (against Milan), he threatens the back line really well. He could have even scored for us today.

‌



“He’s a huge threat to have in your team, if he’s going to stay with us. Obviously the transfer window is still open, but we hope as players that he stays and he’s a big asset to have.

“I’ve played with Marcus for numerous years and I know that from playing against him, and playing with him in training, he is going to help us.”

Rashford enjoyed a fine season in Spain, accumulating 14 goals and 14 assists across 49 appearances in all competitions for Barca.

‌



View 2 Images Rashford is back in the picture at Old Trafford but could still move in the transfer window

Carrick knows all about Rashford's quality having worked with the attacker both as a player and a coach during his previous spells at United.

He hinted earlier this week that he was working on the basis Rashford was staying put, saying: “He's our player and he's come back great. He's just like any other player.

Article continues below

“I've known Marcus a long time and he gives us something a little bit different. And he's been in great spirits since he's been back. He's been back two or three days training and it's just pretty normal, to be honest. And we're looking forward to the start of the season.”
