World.title: PREMIUM TIMES journalist, five others selected for UNCCD COP17 Media Fellowship in Mongolia
World.content:
A journalist with Nigeria’s foremost investigative newspaper, PREMIUM TIMES, has been selected as one of six reporters globally for the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD) COP17 Media Reporting Fellowship.

Abdulkareem Mojeed, a member of the newspaper’s Business and Economy Desk, is the only Nigerian journalist selected for the fellowship, which will support media coverage of the 17th Conference of the Parties (COP17) to the UNCCD in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia.

The other selected journalists are Eric Kasina of Business Daily Africa, Kenya; Shagun Kapil of Down To Earth, India; Ángeles Lucas of El País, Spain; Rafael Cardoso of Agência Brasil, Brazil; and Gonzalo Ortuño of Mongabay Latam, Mexico.

In an email informing Mojeed of his selection, the UNCCD said the fellowship attracted a large number of applications from journalists and media organisations across different regions and languages.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Congratulations. We are pleased to inform you that you have been selected for the UNCCD COP17 Media Reporting Fellowship,” the UNCCD said.

The UNCCD said Mr Mojeed’s application “stood out for the quality of your reporting track record, the strength of your proposed coverage, and your demonstrated commitment to reporting on the interconnected challenges of land, drought and their impact on communities around the world.”

COP17 in Mongolia

The UNCCD COP17 Media Reporting Fellowship is a fully funded programme for journalists to cover the UNCCD’s 17th Conference of the Parties in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia.

According to the United Nations, COP17 is expected to bring together delegates from the UNCCD’s 197 Parties, alongside government, business and civil society leaders, scientists, young people, Indigenous Peoples, pastoralists and smallholder farmers.

Participants will deliberate on solutions to the interconnected challenges of desertification, land degradation and drought, with a focus on how land restoration can help reduce instability, prevent displacement and strengthen human and national security in vulnerable regions.

The UNCCD said COP17 presents a pivotal opportunity for countries and partners to strengthen implementation and mobilise greater investment in drought resilience and sustainable land management.

During the two-week conference, participants are expected to engage in ministerial dialogues, as well as multistakeholder forums and thematic discussions on science-policy integration, innovation and solutions, tools and technologies, and financing.

Beyond the formal negotiations, COP17 is expected to catalyse collective action on rangelands, resilience and water, as well as food systems and soil health.

Reacting to his selection, Mojeed described the fellowship as an opportunity to draw greater attention to the challenges confronting rangelands and grazing routes in Nigeria and across Africa.

“I am truly humbled to have been chosen for this esteemed fellowship. It stands as a testament to the exceptional and impactful journalism we uphold at PREMIUM TIMES.

“I view my selection as a rare opportunity to highlight important stories that will inform the public about how land degradation, drought and desertification are affecting lives and livelihoods of Nigerians, Africans , and beyond, as well as their broader significance when properly addressed.

“I deeply appreciate this recognition and see it as a collective achievement for the entire PT family,” he said.

About Mojeed

Mojeed is a multiple award-winning Business and Environment investigative Journalist. He is a graduate of Botany and Ecological Studies from the University of Uyo, and has brought his science background to bear in Journalism.

He has extensively reported on biodiversity conservation, climate change, agriculture, food security, oil and gas, energy, and power. He has covered major regional and global environmental events, including the African Climate Week, UN Conference of the Parties (COP) and plastics treaty negotiations held in Kenya, Egypt, Dubai, Azerbaijan, and Switzerland.

READ ALSO: PREMIUM TIMES reporter wins 2026 Solution Journalism Award

In 2025, Mojeed was the sole African journalist among the 11 to 12 selected for the esteemed Science, Health, and Environmental Reporting Programme (SHERP) at New York University, with scholarship to pursue studies in the United States. Regrettably, he was unable to participate due to the ongoing stringent visa policies affecting Nigerian and other international applicants worldwide.

His work has earned recognition locally and internationally, with participation in both local and global fellowships including the prestigious SEJ Diversity Fellowship (Philadelphia, USA) and the Y. Eva. Tan Conservation Reporting Fellowship (Mongabay). He is a nature enthusiast. When he is not working, he enjoys travelling, reading, watching and playing soccer.

World.title: ANALYSIS: IReV Performance in the 2026 Osun Governorship Election
World.content:
The performance of the Independent National Electoral Commission’s Result Viewing Portal (IReV) during the 2026 Osun governorship election offers an opportunity to evaluate the platform’s preparedness ahead of the next general election cycle.

IReV was launched to make electronic copies of polling-unit result sheets publicly accessible, providing citizens, political parties, journalists, and election observers with an additional way of tracking the results process and comparing polling-unit records with figures subsequently presented during collation.

Its usefulness, therefore, depends not only on whether results eventually appear on the portal but also on how quickly they become available, how consistently transmission occurs across locations, and how transparently INEC accounts for polling units whose results are not displayed.

The Osun State governorship election involved 3,763 polling units across 30 Local Government Areas and 332 Registration Areas/Wards. CJID monitored IReV throughout the election day and into the following morning, alongside its broader observation of voting, counting, and collation across the state. The pattern showed relatively rapid transmission during the first several hours after voting, a period of slower activity later in the evening, and another substantial increase in uploads overnight.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

How IReV performed in Osun

Results began appearing on IReV while voting and counting were still concluding in parts of the state. At approximately 4:12 p.m. on Saturday, 437 of the expected 3,763 polling-unit results had been uploaded, representing about 11.6 per cent. The number subsequently increased to 849, or 22.56 per cent, and later to 2,463 results, representing 65.45 per cent.

By approximately 9:30 p.m., 3,292 polling-unit results were available, putting statewide coverage at 87.5 per cent and leaving 471 results outstanding. Considering that the official close of polls was 2:30 p.m., and that voting continued beyond that time in polling units where voters remained in the queue, a substantial proportion of the state’s polling-unit results had therefore become publicly accessible within several hours of voting and counting.

Transmission did not progress at the same pace throughout the evening. CJID observed a period when the number of uploaded results remained at 3,292, with the last upload at that stage recorded at approximately 8:48 p.m. Uploading subsequently resumed, with CJID recording 3,482 results at approximately 11:42 p.m., 3,537 shortly afterwards and 3,5,57, shortly after midnight. By 6:55 a.m. on Sunday, 16 August, the figure had reached 3,681, representing 97.82 per cent, and at approximately 7:42 a.m., 3,690 of the expected 3,763 polling-unit results were available, taking statewide coverage to 98.06 per cent.

The progression from 87.5 per cent at 9:30 p.m. to 98.06 per cent the following morning shows that transmission continued substantially overnight,even after the slowdown observed earlier in the evening. It also means that most polling-unit results were publicly available while collation was still underway, which is particularly important for a platform whose principal contribution to the electoral process is the ability it gives the public to independently examine polling-unit records as results move through the collation process.

The statewide figures, however, conceal differences in transmission across LGAs. At one point when statewide uploads were approaching 95 per cent, Irepodun and Ila were already at approximately 99.2 per cent, Ede South and Obokun at about 99 per cent and Boluwaduro at 98.6 per cent. At the other end, Ilesa East stood at approximately 90.9 per cent, Atakumosa West and Ejigbo at about 89.5 per cent, Orolu at 89.4 per cent and Ola-Oluwa at approximately 80.6 per cent.

The gaps narrowed as transmission continued, but their presence suggests that statewide upload percentages alone are insufficient for understanding IReV performance. Differences between LGAs could reflect the timing of poll closure and counting, network availability, BVAS-related issues, geography, security conditions or the conduct of election officials. Establishing which of these factors accounted for slower transmission would require more detailed operational data from INEC, but identifying where delays are concentrated is useful for determining where improvements may be required before subsequent elections.

What happens to the final few percent?

By 7:42 a.m., 73 of Osun’s 3,763 polling units did not have results displayed on IReV. The final governorship result was announced while the portal remained at 98.06 per cent.

IReV is a public result-viewing platform rather than the statutory collation mechanism through which election winners are determined, so the significance of the 73 outstanding polling units lies principally in the completeness of the public record. Once an election has been concluded, citizens examining IReV should ideally be able to understand what happened at every polling unit, including those from which there is no result to display.

CJID’s field reports from Osun illustrate why this requires more information than an upload percentage can provide. In Ife Central, observers reported that voting did not take place in one polling unit following a disagreement over the number of ballot papers supplied, while the result from another polling unit was cancelled following over-voting and the destruction of ballot papers. In circumstances such as these, the absence of a result on IReV may originate from what happened at the polling unit rather than from the transmission system.

The current presentation of IReV provides limited information for making these distinctions. A polling unit where voting was cancelled can appear in much the same way as one where a valid result exists but has not yet been transmitted. Providing a status for polling units without displayed results — whether voting was not conducted, the poll was cancelled, transmission remains pending or another documented circumstance applies — would make the portal considerably more useful for public scrutiny.

This becomes particularly important as IReV approaches complete coverage. At 60 or 70 per cent, the principal question is understandably how quickly the remaining results are being uploaded. At 98 or 99 per cent, attention begins to shift towards the smaller number of polling units that remain unaccounted for, where they are located and why their results are unavailable.

How Osun compares with Anambra, Ekiti

Recent off-cycle governorship elections provide some context for assessing the Osun figures, although the available records differ in what they allow us to measure. CJID tracked the Osun portal repeatedly during election night, providing a progression of uploads over several hours, while the current IReV records for Anambra and Ekiti provide clearer evidence of where those elections eventually settled than of their complete election-night trajectories.

For the 20 June 2026 Ekiti governorship election, IReV currently shows 2,390 results from 2,445 polling units, representing 97.75 per cent of the expected total. The portal records its last upload at 9:19 a.m. on 21 June, the morning after the election. Almost two months later, 55 polling units remain without results displayed on the portal.

The Ekiti LGA figures show that the gap is concentrated more heavily in some in areas than others. Several LGAs are recorded as complete, while Ado Ekiti has 339 results from 344 polling units, has Ikole 183 from 189, has Ijero 138 fr,om 145 and Ekitihas East 95 from 112. The statewide figur,e of 97.75, per cent therefore masks a more pronounced gap in particular parts of the state, with Ekiti East alone accounting for 17 of the polling units without displayed results.

The 8 November 2025 Anambra governorship election is closer to complete coverage. IReV currently shows 5,711 results from 5,720 polling units, representing 99.84 per cent, with nine polling units without displayed results. Most LGAs have complete records, while the remaining gaps are distributed across a limited number of LGAs. The portal also records the most recent upload on 23 November 2025, more than two weeks after election day, showing that the public record continued to change well after the election had concluded.

These records bring out different aspects of IReV performance. Osun gives a clearer picture of transmission speed because CJID followed the portal throughout election night and recorded its movement from 87.5 per cent at 9:30 p.m. to 98.06 per cent the following morning. Anambra shows how close the portal can eventually come to complete coverage, while Ekiti shows how a relatively small statewide gap can persist and become concentrated in particular LGAs.

They also point to the value of separating timeliness from eventual coverage when assessing IReV. Anambra’s current 99.84 per cent is higher than the 98.06 per cent recorded in Osun on the morning after the election, but the current portal does not tell us what proportion of Anambra’s results was available at equivalent points on election night. Similarly, the date of Anambra’s most recent upload tells us that the record continued changing after the election, but not the scale of those later additions. A credible comparative framework therefore requires more systematic publication of upload timestamps and performance data across elections.

The unresolved entries across the three elections also strengthen the case for better polling-unit status information.

Anambra currently has nine polling units without displayed results and Ekiti has 55, while 73 were outstanding in Osun at the point CJID recorded the portal on Sunday morning. The figures themselves cannot explain whether the gaps arose from transmission delays, cancellations, non-conduct of elections or other circumstances. As IReV increasingly records statewide coverage in the high nineties, explaining these remaining entries becomes part of assessing the completeness of the transparency system.

The 2023 experience and what has changed

The public significance attached to these questions is inseparable from the experience of the 2023 presidential election, when IReV became one of the most contested aspects of the results process. INEC subsequently acknowledged that its inability to upload presidential polling-unit results as expected generated widespread criticism and affected public perception of the election, while the Supreme Court observed during subsequent litigation that the malfunction contributed to reduced public confidence.

INEC’s subsequent explanation showed that the problem was more specific than a general collapse of IReV. According to the Commission, National Assembly results were uploading while presidential results encountered a configuration problem related to how the different elections had been mapped within the application.

National Assembly contests were associated with states and constituencies, whereas the presidential election was configured as a single nationwide constituency, creating difficulties when the backend attempted to organise presidential result images according to polling-unit locations.

After technical fixes were introduced, INEC encountered a further problem with a backlog of queued uploads, while some BVAS devices had already been switched off and had to be reconnected before pending transmissions could proceed. The Commission later reported strengthening IReV resilience and introducing additional quality-assurance checks and end-to-end testing.

The recent off-cycle elections suggest a more stable operational environment. Across Anambra, Ekiti and Osun, IReV has been able to publish the overwhelming majority of expected polling-unit results, while the detailed monitoring undertaken in Osun shows that more than 98 per cent were available by the morning after voting. The kind of widespread presidential-result upload problem experienced in 2023 was not observed in Osun.

The scale of a general election, however, is considerably different. Osun involved 3,763 polling units, while INEC’s 2023 post-election review records 176,846 polling units nationwide. A general election also requires electoral infrastructure to operate simultaneously across 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, under widely varying telecommunications, security and logistical conditions, while supporting multiple elections and a much larger number of devices and election personnel.

The experience of 2023 is relevant here because it showed that successful performance under one electoral configuration does not guarantee the same outcome under another. The fact that National Assembly uploads were proceeding while presidential uploads encountered difficulties demonstrates why the performance recorded in state governorship elections cannot by itself establish how IReV will behave during a nationwide general election.

What INEC should address before 2027

The recent elections provide INEC with considerably more operational evidence on which to prepare for 2027 than was available before the last general election. The priority now should be to understand the conditions under which transmission slows, improve the information available about outstanding polling units and test whether the performance recorded in state elections can be sustained under national-scale demand.

One gap exposed by the Osun monitoring is the limited amount of public performance data available from IReV itself. Much of CJID’s assessment depended on repeatedly recording the number of uploaded results at different times. INEC’s backend should contain considerably richer information, including transmission timestamps, unsuccessful upload attempts, retransmissions, processing times and geographical patterns in delays. Publishing an appropriate level of this information after elections would make it possible to distinguish problems associated with the technology from delays caused by late voting, counting, connectivity or other polling-unit circumstances.

INEC could also establish clearer performance benchmarks ahead of 2027, including indicative expectations for the proportion of polling-unit results that should become publicly available within defined periods after counting. Such benchmarks would provide a more consistent basis for evaluating IReV across elections and make it easier to identify when transmission is departing materially from expected performance.

Communication during substantial interruptions also requires attention. When the Osun upload figure remained unchanged at 3,292 for a period during the evening, the public-facing portal offered little indication of what was happening. In a presidential election, a similar period of inactivity would inevitably attract considerably greater scrutiny.

Where INEC identifies a significant technical or operational interruption, timely information about the nature and scope of the problem would reduce uncertainty and allow the public to distinguish a system-wide problem from localised or temporary delays.

The presentation of outstanding polling units should also be improved. Giving every polling unit an identifiable status would allow IReV to distinguish among successfully uploaded results, pending transmissions, cancelled elections, polling units where voting did not take place and other formally recognised circumstances. This would address one of the clearest limitations visible across Osun, Ekiti and Anambra: the portal can show how many results are absent without adequately explaining why they are absent.

The more demanding preparation will be testing IReV under conditions that approximate the 2027 general elections. Stress tests should simulate simultaneous transmission from a volume of devices approaching national election levels, including periods of exceptionally high traffic and transmission from locations with weak or unstable connectivity.

The assessment should cover not only server availability but also processing speed, queued uploads, failed transmissions, retry mechanisms and the ability of the public-facing portal to remain accessible while large volumes of results are being received. Independent technical assessment of this infrastructure before the election would provide an additional basis for evaluating readiness beyond INEC’s own assurances.

Looking towards 2027

The Osun governorship election recorded a strong IReV performance in the period that mattered most for public scrutiny of the results process. Approximately 87.5 per cent of polling-unit results were available by 9:30 p.m., and the figure had reached 98.06 per cent by the following morning, while the portal continued receiving results after the temporary slowdown observed during the evening.

READ ALSO: CJID awards local media sustainability grants to seven Nigerian newsrooms

Recent experience in Anambra and Ekiti also shows that IReV is routinely reaching very high levels of polling-unit coverage in off-cycle governorship elections, although the persistence of outstanding entries demonstrates that near-complete coverage does not always produce a fully explained public record.

The more important question ahead of 2027 is whether these improvements can be reproduced under the scale and complexity of a general election. The next test of IReV will involve far more than keeping the portal online. It will require rapid transmission from a vastly larger number of polling units, consistency across very different parts of the country, clear information when transmission slows, and an ability to account for polling units whose results do not appear.

Nigeria now has several years of practical experience with BVAS and IReV across general and off-cycle elections, including the problems encountered in 2023 and the considerably stronger performance visible in more recent governorship elections. The preparation for 2027 should use that experience to move beyond assurances that the technology will work and towards measurable evidence of how it performs under pressure, where its weaknesses remain and how those weaknesses will be addressed before the next nationwide election.

World.title: Boniface, Chukwueze, Adams shine as Nigerians set Europe aglow ahead of new season
World.content:
Nigerian players across Europe made a strong statement over the weekend, with Akor Adams, Samuel Chukwueze, Victor Boniface, Maduka Okoye, Moses Usor and Rafiu Durosinmi among those who delivered impressive performances for their respective clubs ahead of the 2026/27 season.

From match-winning goals and assists to a long-awaited return from injury, the weekend provided plenty of encouragement for Nigeria’s international stars and those hoping to break into Eric Chelle’s Super Eagles squad.

Adams makes instant impact for Venezia

Akor Adams enjoyed a dream competitive debut for Venezia, scoring twice and providing an assist to inspire a 3-2 comeback victory over Modena in the Coppa Italia on Saturday night.

The Nigerian striker, who joined Venezia from Sevilla during the summer transfer window, immediately showed why the Italian club moved for his services by playing a direct role in all three of their goals.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Giuseppe Ambrosino put Modena ahead, but Adams restored parity in the first half with a composed finish.

Modena regained the advantage after the break through another Ambrosino goal, but Adams once again proved decisive as Venezia mounted their comeback.

With seven minutes remaining, the former Sevilla forward turned provider, setting up John Yeboah to level the score.

Just two minutes later, Adams completed the turnaround himself with a superb strike that put Venezia 3-2 ahead and secured their passage into the next round.

It was an eye-catching competitive debut for Adams, who will now look to build on the performance and establish himself as an important figure for Venezia throughout the new campaign.

Chukwueze stars against Manchester United

Samuel Chukwueze also produced a performance to remember, scoring once and providing two assists as AC Milan defeated Manchester United 4-2 in a pre-season friendly on Saturday.

The Super Eagles winger played the entire match and responded brilliantly after United took the lead inside the opening two minutes through Harry Maguire.

Chukwueze restored parity by calmly converting from a lay-off by Goncalo Ramos.

Patrick Dorgu put United back in front six minutes into the second half, but Chukwueze again made his presence felt.

The Nigerian set up Alphadjo Cisse for Milan’s equaliser before providing another assist for Ramos to head the Italian giants into the lead.

Ruben Loftus-Cheek later completed the scoring for Milan.

The impressive outing will come as a major boost for Chukwueze, who will be hoping to continue his progress and repay the faith shown in him by manager Ruben Amorim following his successful loan spell at Fulham last season.

Boniface seals Leverkusen victory

Victor Boniface was also on target, scoring a late winner as Bayer Leverkusen defeated Newcastle United 2-1 in a pre-season friendly at St James’ Park as part of the VisitMalta Weekender.

Leverkusen needed just one minute to take the lead, with Ibrahim Maza firing a superb 25-yard effort past the Newcastle goalkeeper.

Malick Thiaw equalised for the hosts shortly before half-time, but Boniface settled the contest eight minutes from full-time with a fine finish to hand Leverkusen victory.

The goal represents another encouraging step for the 25-year-old, who is determined to rediscover his best form after difficult campaigns in 2024/25 and 2025/26.

His loan spell at Werder Bremen was particularly frustrating, having been interrupted by a serious knee injury that required surgery in January and limited him to just 11 Bundesliga appearances without a goal.

Leverkusen head coach Carles Martinez believes the striker is moving in the right direction.

“He knows what he has to do. I’m pushing him as well. It’s getting better. His quality is obvious,” Martinez said.

Boniface, meanwhile, expressed his appreciation to Leverkusen supporters for their backing during his difficult period.

“The fans supported me in good times and bad times, and I really appreciate that. We, players, need their support. I’m really very happy and thank every single one of them,” he said.

Okoye returns with a clean sheet

Maduka Okoye also made a positive return to competitive action, keeping a clean sheet as Udinese defeated Padova 1-0 in their Coppa Italia opener.

The Nigerian goalkeeper had earlier been declared fit for the fixture by Udinese coach Kosta Runjaic.

Okoye had been sidelined after suffering a shoulder injury during Udinese’s pre-season training camp in Lienz, Austria, which ran from July 22 to early August.

His return to full training came in time for the Coppa Italia fixture, allowing the 26-year-old to reclaim his place between the posts and begin the new campaign with a shutout.

Usor strengthens Super Eagles’ case

Moses Usor was another Nigerian who caught the eye, producing a scintillating performance in LASK’s 4-1 Austrian Bundesliga victory over Austria Wien.

The 24-year-old winger was involved in almost everything positive for his side.

Usor set up Samuel Adeniran for LASK’s equaliser before scoring himself to put the hosts ahead.

He then combined with Adeniran again to create the striker’s second goal before providing a fourth assist for Christoph Lang.

Usor was substituted after 63 minutes, but his contribution had already made a significant impact.

He has now registered two goals and two assists in three competitive matches this season, a run that is increasingly strengthening calls for Super Eagles coach Eric Chelle to hand him an opportunity during the next international window.

Durosinmi continues scoring form

Rafiu Durosinmi also continued his impressive start to the campaign, scoring from the penalty spot for Genk on Saturday.

The goal means the 25-year-old has now scored twice in his opening two matches of the season.

Durosinmi has already set his sights on winning the Belgian Pro League Golden Boot this season and will hope to follow in the footsteps of fellow Nigerians Paul Onuachu and Tolu Arokodare.

Both compatriots have previously finished as the Belgian top flight’s leading scorer, with Arokodare claiming the honour after scoring 21 league goals for Genk during the 2024/25 season.

With the 2026/27 campaign only beginning, the early signs are certainly encouraging for Nigeria’s players across Europe.

World.title: Davido celebrates Adeleke’s victory in Osun governorship election
World.content:
Afrobeats singer David Adeleke, popularly known as Davido, has celebrated the re-election of his uncle, Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke, describing the outcome of Saturday’s governorship election as a victory for the family.

The singer shared his reaction on Sunday in a post on his X account shortly after the governor was declared the winner of the election.

“We did it, Unc (Uncle),” Davido wrote.

In the accompanying video, Davido was seen lying on the floor as one of his aides, Israel, congratulated him.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The singer had been actively involved in his uncle’s campaign ahead of the election and repeatedly expressed support for the governor during the campaign period.

His latest celebration came immediately after the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) formally declared Mr Adeleke the winner of the Osun governorship election.

PREMIUM TIMES had earlier reported that the State Returning Officer, Joshua Ogunwole, declared the result at the INEC State Collation Centre in Osogbo on Sunday morning.

Mr Adeleke, who contested on the platform of the Accord Party, polled 511,067 votes to defeat his closest challenger, Bola Oyebamiji of the All Progressives Congress (APC), who secured 444,815 votes.

The result gave Mr Adeleke a winning margin of 66,252 votes.

The governor won in 19 of the state’s 30 local government areas, while Mr Oyebamiji secured victory in the remaining 11.

Mr Adeleke’s victories included Ede North, Ede South, Ejigbo, Iwo, Egbedore, Ife North, Ife East, Ife Central, Oriade, Ifelodun, Orolu, Aiyedaade, Aiyedire, Odo-Otin, Boluwaduro, Ilesa West, Ifedayo, Osogbo and Ila.

Mr Oyebamiji won in Ilesa East, Boripe, Irepodun, Obokun, Atakunmosa West, Irewole, Atakunmosa East, Isokan, Ola-Oluwa, Ife South and Olorunda.

The African Democratic Congress candidate, Najeem Salaam, came third with 17,180 votes.

According to the final figures announced by the returning officer, 1,010,684 voters were accredited for the election, while 985,079 votes were valid.

A total of 20,721 votes were rejected, bringing the total votes cast to 1,005,800.

Mr Ogunwole, the vice-chancellor of the Federal University, Oye-Ekiti, subsequently returned Mr Adeleke, who was elected after the results were collated and party agents signed the final result.

The declaration secured another four-year term for the incumbent governor, who first won the Osun governorship election in 2022.

Davido, whose support for his uncle has been prominent throughout the political contest, has previously used his public platform to campaign for Mr Adeleke.

World.title: Nigeria targets local production of armoured vehicles, anti-drone systems
World.content:
By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto

Nigeria is stepping up efforts to break its longstanding dependence on imported military hardware as the Defence Industries Corporation of Nigeria D7G (DICON-D7G) advances plans to establish local production lines for armoured vehicles, anti-drone platforms and other specialised defence equipment.

The ambitious initiative, being pursued in partnership with Eagles International for Defence Systems, is expected to deepen technology transfer, expand Nigeria’s indigenous defence manufacturing capacity, create thousands of direct and indirect employment opportunities and strengthen the country’s strategic capacity to respond to emerging security threats.

The development was disclosed in a statement signed by the Chief Executive Officer of DICON-D7G, Mr Osman Chennar, following a two-day inspection tour of factories and military production facilities in Cairo by the Minister of State for Defence, Dr Bello Mohammed Matawalle, and his delegation.

During the inspection, the Nigerian delegation assessed various defence production systems and platforms being considered as part of efforts to establish and expand local manufacturing capabilities for the Nigerian Armed Forces.

Chennar said the partnership would facilitate the transfer of advanced military technologies to Nigeria and create production lines capable of manufacturing a wide range of military platforms locally, with the long-term prospect of positioning the country to export defence equipment to other African nations.

According to him, the initial phase of the collaboration is expected to create employment for more than 200 workers, while providing opportunities for about 100 retired military personnel whose experience and technical expertise could be deployed in the emerging defence-industrial ecosystem.

Among the platforms targeted for local production are the Armoured Multi-Purpose Vehicle BR6, a modular multi-mission defence platform; Armoured Personnel Carrier cabins; 120mm manual mortar launcher cabins; and specialised medical evacuation and ambulance cabins.

The proposed production portfolio also includes the MRAP Buffalo U.10 and M.12 armoured vehicles, MRAP-Buffalo F-4, Rhino Guard GXR anti-drone and RPG-protected vehicle, APC Moon PT6, GXR Phantom light vehicle and BMP-2 Infantry Fighting Vehicle.

The development comes amid Nigeria’s sustained efforts to strengthen indigenous defence manufacturing as the country confronts persistent security challenges, including terrorism, banditry, kidnapping and other asymmetric threats that have placed enormous demands on the Armed Forces.

Already, the Nigerian Army has begun taking delivery of locally manufactured armoured vehicles, signalling a gradual shift from heavy reliance on foreign procurement towards the development of a domestic defence production chain capable of supporting military operations.

Beyond the manufacture of military platforms, DICON-D7G is also planning the development of a dedicated military jetty in Lagos to strengthen the logistics backbone of Nigeria’s emerging defence industrial complex.

Chennar said the proposed facility would serve as a strategic logistics and distribution hub for the movement of raw materials, components and finished military equipment within Nigeria and potentially across the African continent. He added that the military jetty is expected to create employment for more than 200 retired military personnel and over 1,000 civilians when the project becomes operational.

The planned expansion of indigenous defence production is expected to have far-reaching implications for Nigeria’s economy and national security, including reducing exposure to foreign supply disruptions, retaining defence expenditure within the domestic economy, developing specialised technical manpower and building industrial capacity capable of sustaining the military during prolonged security operations.

The DICON-D7G and Eagles International partnership is therefore being positioned as more than an equipment procurement arrangement, but as a strategic attempt to build a sustainable Nigerian defence-industrial ecosystem capable of designing, assembling, manufacturing and maintaining critical military platforms while eventually competing for a share of the expanding African defence market.

World.title: Plateau police arrest officer over shooting of trader
World.content:
By Golok Nanmwa

The Plateau State Police Command has arrested and detained a police officer who allegedly shot an unarmed trader in the leg at a checkpoint in Riyom Local Government Area of the state.

The incident occurred on August 11 when the trader, identified as Danladi, who moves goods with his van, was stopped at a checkpoint while conveying vegetables to the Southeast.

The Police Public Relations Officer, PPRO, of the Plateau State Police Command, Superintendent Alfred Alabo, confirmed that the officer involved had been disarmed and taken into custody.

Alabo said the Divisional Police Officer, DPO, in charge of the Riyom Division, immediately mobilised to the scene after receiving information about the incident, disarmed the officer and took him to the State Criminal Investigation Department, CID.

He said the officer was currently undergoing questioning and a disciplinary process over the incident.

“The DPO, Riyom Division, came there immediately.

He got the information with his men, disarmed the officer and also took him immediately to the State CID, where he is currently undergoing questioning and a disciplinary process,” Alabo said.

According to him, the Commissioner of Police has also directed the DPO to visit the hospital where the victim is receiving treatment and provide feedback on his condition.

“Concerning the victim, the CP has directed the DPO to go to the hospital and see how the victim is faring and give us feedback. A lot is ongoing concerning that,” he said.

The PPRO stressed that the investigation into the circumstances surrounding the shooting was ongoing, assuring the public that the command would provide updates as the process progresses.

“The officer is with us; he is in custody at the State CID. Investigations are ongoing,” he said.

Alabo, however, appealed to members of the public to avoid confrontations with armed security personnel whenever disagreements occur, urging them to use established complaint channels to report alleged misconduct.

He particularly appealed to motorists and other road users to remain calm when stopped at checkpoints and report any alleged misconduct by security personnel through the appropriate authorities.

“When an officer misbehaves on the road, don’t try to attack or confront them while they are armed with a rifle. Please, make use of our numbers,” he said.

He explained that the police had established mechanisms through which members of the public could report misconduct by officers, including the Police Public Relations Office, the Police Complaint Response Unit and other designated complaint channels.

“If you feel that any officer has gone against or attacked your fundamental human right in any way, report it to the appropriate authority.

“If you don’t even know how to go about it, just call the phone number of the PPRO and report, and I can assure you we will do something about it,” Alaba said.

The PPRO urged members of the public not to allow anger to result in physical confrontation with armed security personnel, saying such actions could further escalate an already tense situation.

He said both sides of the incident were being investigated, noting that while the command was aware of the allegation against the police officer, the officer also had his own account of what transpired.

According to him, the command would establish the facts of the matter through its investigation.

Alabo further disclosed that the officers involved in the incident were not originally from the Plateau State Police Command but were in the state to perform certain duties under the supervision of the Commissioner of Police.

He assured the public that appropriate disciplinary action was already being taken against the officer.

“Concerning that investigation, it is still ongoing. The officer’s disciplinary measures are being taken already, and we want to assure the general public that this will not happen again,” he said.

The command appealed to members of the public to remain calm, assuring them that the matter was being handled and that the public would be updated as the investigation progresses.

World.title: ‘I wish him great success’ — Tinubu congratulates Adeleke, commends INEC

By Bayo Wahab

President Bola Tinubu has congratulated Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, on his victory in the August 15 governorship election, wishing him success as he begins another four-year term.

Reacting to the election outcome, Tinubu in a statement personally signed by him and posted on X, said Adeleke’s re-election demonstrated the confidence the people of Osun State had in his leadership.

“I called Governor Ademola Adeleke earlier today to congratulate him on his election victory in Osun State. His victory once again confirmed the confidence the people of Osun State have in him,” the President said.

“I wish him great success as he prepares to lead the state for the next four years,” Tinubu said.

The President also charged Adeleke to use his renewed mandate to promote development and stability across the state.

“Now that he has won, Governor Adeleke must unite the people of Osun State and rally them for growth, stability, and social and economic progress, regardless of the political choices they made at the election,” he said.

He concluded by expressing hope that the country’s democratic institutions would continue to grow stronger.

World.title: Arsenal face Man City in Community Shield as Maresca begins new era
World.content:
Arsenal and Man City will begin their 2026/27 campaign on Sunday when they take on each other in the Community Shield at Cardiff’s Principality Stadium.

The clash, scheduled for 3pm UK time, pits last season’s Premier League champions against a Manchester City side entering a new era following Pep Guardiola’s departure.

Mikel Arteta will be aiming to start the new campaign with silverware, while City’s new manager Enzo Maresca will look to mark his first competitive game in charge with a statement victory.

Maresca, who previously worked under Guardiola as Manchester City’s under-21 manager, has inherited a squad that has undergone major changes during the summer.

Bernardo Silva has moved to Real Madrid, while John Stones and Manuel Akanji have also left the club. Nathan Ake joined Fenerbahce, Tijjani Reijnders is set to move to Al Qadsiah and goalkeeper James Trafford has joined Leeds United.

City’s biggest signing so far has been Nottingham Forest midfielder Elliott Anderson, who arrived for a reported British-record £116 million fee. Geronimo Rulli has also joined as a backup goalkeeper, while the club has recruited several young prospects.

City’s pre-season included a 1-1 draw with Inter Milan in Hong Kong before victories over the K League All Stars and Atletico Madrid in South Korea.

Arteta is confident his players are ready for the opening fixture and is targeting another Community Shield triumph.

“I love the way the players have come back, most of them earlier than expected, really fit with all the testing, and they all seem in great condition,” Arteta said.

“The best version of us has to be on Sunday, and that’s the intention: that we have the best performance and the best way to start the season, by lifting the first trophy.”

Maresca, meanwhile, insists City will treat the match as a competitive final rather than a pre-season friendly.

“For me personally, it is a trophy. When trophies and a final are there, you always try to win the game, so no friendly game at all,” he said.

“Arsenal have shown in the last five years that they have always been there. It’s a fantastic team, well managed by Mikel. Last year they won the Premier League; they showed how good they are at this moment, but at the same time, we are City and we are going to try to close the gap and try to compete again.”

Arsenal will be without William Saliba and Jurrien Timber. Saliba is recovering from a back problem, while Timber remains sidelined with the groin injury that ruled him out of the World Cup.

Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi have yet to feature in pre-season but have returned to training and could be involved.

City could also be without several players who went deep into the World Cup, including Erling Haaland, Marc Guehi, Nico O’Reilly, Rayan Cherki, Jeremy Doku and Anderson.

Rodri will miss the match after undergoing minor back surgery, while Ryan McAidoo is sidelined with a shoulder injury. Jack Grealish, meanwhile, has returned to training after spending last season on loan at Everton.

Arsenal have a strong record in the Community Shield, having won the competition 17 times, including shared victories. They have also won their last five appearances in the curtain-raiser.

The Gunners have beaten Manchester City in all three previous Community Shield meetings, winning 4-0 in 1934, 3-0 in 2014 and on penalties after a 1-1 draw in 2023.

Arteta has also won all four of his previous Community Shield appearances, twice as a player and twice as Arsenal manager.

Sunday’s match will be decided by a penalty shootout if the score is level after 90 minutes, with no extra time to be played.

Sam Barrott will referee the contest, assisted by Craig Taylor and Blake Antrobus, while Farai Hallam will serve as fourth official and James Bell will oversee VAR.

World.title: Triumph against tyranny:  Dickson, Keyamo, Murray-Bruce, Dino, Rhodes-Vivour congratulate Adeleke
World.content:
File: Governor Ademola Adeleke

By Nwafor Sunday

Former Bayelsa State Governor, Henry Seriake Dickson; Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo; former Senator Ben Murray-Bruce; and other political figures have congratulated Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, on his victory in Saturday’s governorship election.

The politicians, in separate messages on X on Sunday, described Adeleke’s re-election as significant for democracy and the people of Osun State, while urging political actors to draw lessons from the outcome.

Dickson: Victory reminder of people’s democratic power

Dickson congratulated Adeleke on his re-election, saying the outcome demonstrated that the people could still assert their democratic will through the ballot despite the challenges facing the political environment.

“I warmly congratulate the Governor of Osun State, His Excellency Senator Ademola Adeleke, on his victory in the Osun State Governorship Election.

“This victory is significant not only for Governor Adeleke and the people of Osun State, but also for our democracy. It is a reminder that, even in an increasingly challenging political environment, the people can still assert their democratic will through the ballot,” he said.

The former governor commended Osun voters for standing firm in defence of their democratic choice.

He also called on candidates who lost the election to support Adeleke in the interest of peace and development in the state.

“I commend the people of Osun State for standing firm in defence of their democratic choice, and call on all those who contested the election and emerged on the losing side to join hands with the Governor in the spirit of sportsmanship and work for the peace and development of Osun State,” Dickson said.

He wished Adeleke and the people of Osun continued peace, progress and prosperity.

Keyamo congratulates Adeleke

Keyamo also congratulated Adeleke on what he described as a historic victory in the governorship election.

“Huge congratulations to Governor Ademola Adeleke on his historic victory in the governorship election in Osun State,” the minister said.

Murray-Bruce: Congratulations, my brother

Murray-Bruce congratulated Adeleke, whom he described as a friend and former colleague in the eighth Senate.

“Warm congratulations to my dear friend and former colleague in the 8th Senate, Governor Ademola Adeleke, on his victory in the Osun State governorship election.

“Congratulations, my brother,” he said.

Rhodes-Vivour: Osun triumph against tyranny

Former Lagos State Labour Party governorship candidate, Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour, congratulated Osun voters, describing the election outcome as a triumph against what he termed tyranny.

“I congratulate the great people of Osun on their spectacular triumph against tyranny,” he said.

Rhodes-Vivour said the outcome demonstrated that intimidation and financial inducements could not deter determined voters.

“You have proven that no amount of guns, intimidation and inducement can deter a people determined not to return under the yoke of their oppressors,” he said.

He urged Nigerians to draw lessons from the Osun election ahead of the 2027 general elections.

“Let us take the lessons from Osun and build on it towards the general elections,” Rhodes-Vivour added.

Dino Melaye: Opposition wins in Osun

Former Kogi State senator, Dino Melaye, also congratulated Adeleke, describing the outcome as an opposition victory.

“Opposition win in Osun. Congratulations Ademola Adeleke. We are dancing to the Villa. APC… odabo,” Melaye posted.

Adeleke was declared winner of the election after polling 511,067 votes to defeat his closest challenger, Bola Oyebamiji of the All Progressives Congress (APC), who scored 444,815 votes.

World.title: FG: Diaspora, Strategic Partnerships Critical to Nigeria’s Security, Prosperity
World.content:
Michael Olugbode in Abuja

The Federal Government has declared that Nigeria’s growing engagement with its diaspora and strategic international partners will be central to its efforts to strengthen national security, expand economic opportunities and drive sustainable development.

Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Sola Enikanolaiye, stated this at the Dinner Night of the Nigerian Diaspora Economic Conference in Toronto, Canada, where he outlined the government’s approach to security, diaspora engagement and Nigeria’s emerging strategic partnerships.

Enikanolaiye said security remained one of the country’s major challenges, adding that the administration of President Bola Tinubu was deploying every available means to contain the security threats that had confronted Nigeria for more than a decade.

“Security remains a major challenge, but the current administration is doing everything humanly possible to ensure that we contain these that have been with us in multifaceted manner for the past 10 or so years,” he said.

The minister disclosed that Nigeria was entering what he described as a “new era of partnership of strategic autonomy” with key international partners, including the United States.

He revealed that he had just returned from Washington, where he participated in high-level engagements with American officials.

“I came in from Washington only yesterday. I was privileged to have been part of the team meeting with the Americans,” he said.

According to him, the renewed engagement is designed to produce tangible benefits for Nigerians rather than merely symbolic diplomatic relationships.

He said the objective was to secure “core, concrete, positive outcomes for Nigerians in terms of security, in terms of prosperity, in terms of defence and the welfare of the Nigerian people”.

The minister’s remarks come as Nigeria continues to deepen international cooperation on security, economic development and strategic interests, while seeking partnerships that reflect the country’s national priorities.

A major focus of the minister’s address was the Federal Government’s renewed emphasis on the Nigerian diaspora as a strategic resource.

He said the Tinubu administration no longer viewed Nigerians living abroad primarily through the lens of consular responsibilities and government assistance.

“For this government, Nigerians in the diaspora are critical assets of national development,” Enikanolaiye said.

“We don’t see you as a basket case of consular burden responsibilities always in need of government’s intervention and assistance. No.”

Instead, he said, the government regarded Nigerians abroad as a pool of highly skilled human resources whose expertise, capital, networks and international experience could contribute significantly to Nigeria’s development priorities.

“On the contrary, we see you as a vital human resource with huge capacities for Nigeria which government is trying to harness in terms of our national development priorities,” he added.

Enikanolaiye also challenged Nigerians at home and abroad to confront the divisions that continue to undermine national cohesion and economic cooperation.

He acknowledged the existence of a “trust deficit” among Nigerians, particularly within diaspora communities, but urged citizens to deliberately move beyond ethnic, religious and tribal considerations.

“We are aware of the trust deficit that exists among Nigerians especially those of us abroad. Let’s try and break those barriers of ethnicity, barriers of religion, barriers of tribe,” he said.

He urged Nigerians to focus instead on cooperation capable of generating production, development, growth and prosperity.

“Let’s relate on the functional aspect of cooperation that promotes production, that promotes development, that promotes growth and prosperity unto Nigerian,” the minister added.

The minister also acknowledged Canada’s contribution to Nigeria’s development and called for stronger partnerships based on mutual respect and cooperation.

He said Nigeria remained committed to working with Canada and other international partners to build relationships capable of delivering practical benefits to both sides.

Enikanolaiye commended the organisers of the Nigerian Diaspora Economic Conference and members of the diaspora community for their contribution to Nigeria’s development.

He described the conference as an important platform for celebrating the Nigerian diaspora as an asset to the country and reaffirmed the Federal Government’s readiness to collaborate with Nigerians abroad and international partners in advancing Nigeria’s national interests.

The minister’s message was clear: Nigeria’s security, prosperity and development will increasingly depend not only on domestic efforts but also on the strategic mobilisation of its global Nigerian community and partnerships built around mutual respect, shared interests and tangible outcomes.

World.title: Gov Adeleke Seeks Post-Election Peace, Promises Dev’t, Good Governance
World.content:
Yinka Kolawole in Osogbo

Osun State Governor Ademola Ademola has appealed for restoration of peace and unity among the people to heal the wounds of pre-election violence even as he promised to expand state development and widen the nets of good governance.

Addressing the media after his election victory at the Saturday governorship election, the governor warned against post-election attacks on rivals and avoidance of counter-attacks from old wounds, urging forgiveness and restoration of communal love after weeks of gun attacks across the state.

While observing a minute silence for victims of the pre-election violence, the re-elected governor tasked community leaders and traditional institutions to embark on peace building in their communities as “the issues are settled by the grace of God and people”.

The governor, who dedicated his victory at the polls to God and the people of the state, commended the resilience, the strong will and unwavering commitment to democracy of the people, promising not to disappoint them.

“As you have trusted me with a second term in office, I will reinforce my strong points and correct my errors. Osun will witness further accelerated development and growth under my renewed five-point agenda,” the governor reassured the people.

The governor further commended “Mr President, His Excellency, Senator Bola Ahemd Tinubu for his strong support for a free and fair election”, declaring that “Mr President is a son of Osun State, and I hereby reaffirm my earlier endorsement of him for a second term in the 2027 presidential election”.

“To all lovers of democracy, I thank you for supporting our struggle. From home and abroad, the support is overwhelming. My faith in democracy is deepened.

“Most importantly, I thank the media for standing by us. The constant coverage in support of democracy emboldened us. We are grateful. Osun State is on the march again. We shall expand development, and widen the net of good governance,

“In this race, there is no victor, no vanquished. I extend olive branch to my co-contestants. I am the governor of all Osun people,” adding that: “My vision remains taking Osun from a civil service state to an industrial state and an investment destination.”

A total of 3,292 polling unit results have been uploaded to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) IReV portal, representing 87.48 per cent of the 3,763 expected results in the ongoing Osun State election.

The figure was recorded as of 8:48pm on Saturday, August 15, 2026, as the electronic uploading of results from polling units continued.

The IReV portal provides a platform for the public to view polling unit results uploaded during elections, offering greater transparency in the results transmission process.

The number of uploaded results is expected to increase as more results from polling units across the state are uploaded.

A total of 3,029 polling unit results have been uploaded to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) IReV portal, representing 80.49 per cent of the 3,763 expected results in the ongoing Osun State election.

6 05PM

INEC Materials Distroyed By Hoodlums as Voters Run for Safety in Ejigbo, ADC Candidate, Salaam, Reacts

Yinka Kolawole in Osogbo

At unit 13 ward 4 in Ejigbo local government area of Osun State, polling unit of the ADC governorship candidate, Rt. Hon. Najeem Salaams was disrupted by political thugs as all INEC materials were destroyed completely.

Also voters at the polling unit ran away for their safety.

However, while reacting after the attack, ADC candidate, Dr Najeem Salaam, said “There was a total disruption of the electoral process and their plan was to attack me.

According to him, “That was an attempt to attack me personally. It was my strategic movement away from that area that made it impossible for them to attack me. Of course, my security personnel protected me and helped me get out of the area.”

“So, it is not a small thing; it is a big issue. This was a well-planned attack. And why did it happen immediately after I cast my vote? People had been voting before I arrived to cast my own vote. It happened immediately afterwards, and because of the strength I have in my unit, I did not just wait around.”

“I feel so bad and sad about it. I am worried and disturbed about the state of Nigerian democracy, the way we are going, and the way security operations are being handled. What does the future hold for everybody in this country?”

“It appears that when you belong to a particular party or have the backing of the government, you can do things the way you want. This is not fair. This is not democracy.”

“A lot of people ran for their lives. I wish you had the pictures and captions to show it. Elderly women and men ran away to save their lives. So, how can one be happy with this?”

“The citizens needed protection and assistance, but they were not getting the help they needed. It is worrisome and disturbing. That is it.”

“The security officials have arrested one of them, and I hope and believe he is still in their custody. We will pursue this afterwards because, in an attempt on my life, I cannot close my eyes, remain calm or stay silent about it. I will follow it up and escalate the matter.”

“Even after the election, the person needs to be questioned. Why was this done? Was it really targeted at me?”

” I can see that the Security Agencies were just looking. The security officers were just watching, and I think it is expected because they may be conniving with certain political parties.”

“They were just looking. That is why sometimes people take the law into their own hands and do things, and that is how we normally have crises in our society.”

“If we really want to protect the democracy that we are all yearning for, this is not the way to go.People are being denied. This is the use of force. I said somewhere, how can we differentiate this from military rule? When people vote and their votes do not count, what is all the preparation for? Why are we campaigning?”

“This is not an election; it is a selection. You want people who want to be in power, and then you select them. That is exactly what they are doing.”

“We appeal to whoever they are and whoever is listening to heed this call. This is not the way. You are in power today; you will not be there tomorrow. What legacy are we leaving for them,

Which direction are we giving to the people who are coming behind us?” Salam noted.

EU Observer Hub Reports 38 Security Incidents, 323 Electoral Offences

Yinka Kolawole in Osogbo

The European Union Support to Democratic Governance in Nigeria Election Observation Hub (EU-SDGN EOH) says it recorded 38 security incidents and 323 cases of electoral offences and irregularities in the 726 polling units monitored as of 12 noon on Saturday, as voting held in the Osun State off-cycle governorship election.

A preliminary statement issued this evening said, “the Hub, made up of the Centre for Media and Society (CEMESO), the International Press Centre (IPC), the Nigerian Women Trust Fund (NWTF), TAF Africa, The Kukah Centre (TKC) and Yiaga Africa, said it deployed 823 accredited observers across polling units in all 30 local government areas to monitor the election, which was contested by 15 candidates.”

“Of 2,339,233 registered voters, 1,906,390, representing 81.50 percent, had collected their Permanent Voters Cards and were eligible to vote, the Hub said.”

On the security incidents, the Hub reported 25 cases of thuggery, 12 attacks on electoral officials and 9 cases of voter intimidation by security personnel.

“It separately recorded 323 cases of electoral offences across the polling units observed, including 103 cases of vote trading, 85 cases of exposure of ballot papers, 31 cases of obstruction of voters, 38 cases of campaigning at polling units, 28 cases of inducement of polling and security officials, 14 cases of voter impersonation, 12 cases of multiple voting and 7 cases of misconduct by election officials.”

The Hub noted that the figures do not correspond to 323 individual polling units, as multiple offences were recorded at some locations.

The Hub also flagged specific cases of voter intimidation by security agents at PU 29-10-10-005, Igbon District Council School, Ejigbo, and PU 29-30-06-015, opposite No. 22 Oke Ola Street, Okanla Area, Osogbo.

“On the accreditation process, 608 of 726 observed polling units, or 83.7 percent, had polling officials with a full complement of both sensitive and non-sensitive materials between 7:30am and 8:00am. A further 75 polling units opened between 8:00am and 8:30am, and 42 between 8:30am and 11:00am, while one polling unit remained unopened as of 11:00am due to non-arrival of personnel and materials.”

The Hub said 58 Bimodal Voter Accreditation System devices malfunctioned in the polling units observed, of which 41 were subsequently fixed and accreditation resumed.

The Hub reported voter turnout as impressive, with women accounting for about 59 percent of turnout in observed polling units and more than 70 percent turnout among persons with disabilities at 12 designated PWD-friendly polling units. Women made up 36 percent of polling officials deployed.

The Hub’s fact-checkers said they had verified 11 false claims circulating about alleged payment of INEC officials, arrests by police and underage voting as of the time of the report, while claims relating to shooting and disruption of voting were still being verified.

The statement is a preliminary account covering the process up to 12 noon and will be followed by a full Post-Election Report after collation and declaration of results, the Hub said.

It urged political parties and candidates to pursue grievances through lawful and judicial channels in line with the Peace Accord signed on 30 July, and called for calm as the process moves toward conclusion.
