Tech.title: Disney’s Millennium Falcon Ride Activates Fortnite In-Game Rewards
Tech.content:
The next Fortnite tie-in is here, and it’s connected with a real-world experience: jump on the Millennium Falcon: Smugglers Run ride at either Disneyland or Disney World starting from Sunday, Aug. 16, and you’ll earn exclusive in-game extras.

Unveiled by Disney and Epic Games during the annual D23 convention in Anaheim on Saturday night, you’ll be able to use the official Disneyland apps to accept a special mission on the interactive ride to collect crates for your Fortnite account. You can use the crates to earn rewards on a new custom Star Wars island in the game called Smugglers Gambit.

“Smugglers Gambit, built in-house by an incredibly talented team, is an immersive, high-quality game,” said Sean Shoptaw, EVP of Disney Games and Digital Entertainment. “These experiences reflect our ambition to connect stories and worlds across formats into one converged entertainment ecosystem.”

On Smugglers Gambit, you can play as a smuggler from the Outer Rim (the location represented by Galaxy’s Edge at the Disney Parks). You’ll be able to explore the new Star Wars locations of Ord Ryla and Mersa Veta Station on the new island.

It’ll have co-op missions, quests, class choices, leveling up and new gear available to unlock. You’ll be battling pirates, as well as “Imperial remnants and dangerous wildlife.”

The Millennium Falcon ride opened at Disneyland and Disney World with the launch of the Star Wars-themed areas in 2019. It allows six people to ride inside a cockpit replica of Han Solo’s famous spaceship, with two people serving as pilots, two as gunners and two as engineers to steer the ship, blast enemies away and repair any damage received to the ship during the flight, respectively.

It’s a flight simulator, so you watch a screen take you through one of several scenarios (the latest Mandalorian-themed missions just launched to tie in with the release of The Mandalorian and Grogu in cinemas in May) while the ride vehicle moves in tandem, and you use physical controls to interact with and affect the flight.

The cockpit technology was built on Unreal Engine 5 and developed by Walt Disney Imagineering together with Industrial Light & Magic, the famed visual effects studio founded by Star Wars creator George Lucas in the 1970s.

Smugglers Gambit was similarly built with Imagineering, Lucasfilm and Disney Games, expanding the story of Hondo Ohnaka, the pirate, smuggler and eventual Resistance ally based at the Black Spire Outpost on Batuu. Ohnaka first appeared in the Clone Wars TV show, but is best known as a shady ally of the protagonists in the follow-up cartoon series, Rebels.

“Building on Epic’s technology, Disney’s Imagineers are shaping the future of interactive entertainment, where an experience goes from the physical world into Fortnite,” said Epic Games President Adam Sussman.

Millennium Falcon: Smugglers Run | Fortnite costs nothing, other than your pricey theme park entry, and only requires you to accept the special mission via the Disneyland app or My Disney Experience app while you’re waiting in line for the ride. You then need to link your MyDisney account with your Epic Games account to claim your rewards in Fortnite, or use a code to transfer them from the ride to the game.

“The seamless link between Millennium Falcon: Smugglers Run and Smugglers Gambit … (is) a groundbreaking example of how stories can flow across screens, theme park rides and games,” said James Waugh, Senior Vice President, Franchise Story & Creative Strategy, Lucasfilm.

The ride tie-in follows the Star Wars IP Toolkit’s launch in Fortnite in May — which Disney says drew in 8 million players in the first 72 hours — an expansion that allows players to build their own Star Wars-themed games and islands in Fortnite. The game also famously hosted an event back in Dec. 2019 that heralded the return of Emperor Palpatine a week ahead of his appearance in Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker.

Theme parks have been leaning increasingly into more immersive experiences, with Universal Studios Orlando last year opening Epic Universe, which, among other experiences, lets you use your Super Nintendo World Power-Up bands as Amiibo on your Nintendo Switch. The Smugglers Run Fortnite experience looks to be the first one that gives you in-game rewards back home, depending on how well you play a theme park game.

Tech.title: Lego Star Wars: The Mandalorian Is Packed With Laughs, Flashbacks and Lots of Grogu
Tech.content:
Star Wars is at its best when it doesn’t take itself too seriously, and there’s no greater example of this than Lego Star Wars. The franchise, complete with its own video game on multiple platforms, prides itself on delivering a cute story with loads of laughs and inside jokes just for the biggest fans.

Fast on the heels of The Mandalorian and Grogu leaving theaters and hitting Disney Plus, the duo and a lot of their friends are getting a Lego Star Wars film just about them. And if you happened to be at D23, there was a chance to watch the whole thing early.

Dropping on Disney Plus September 2nd, Lego Star Wars: The Mandalorian is a hilarious trip down memory lane done Lego style. Recaps of the entire Mandalorian story so far, plus or minus some embellishments from the storytellers take up the one hour special in a way that kept me laughing the entire time. Keep an ear out for some of the original actors from the series showing up to voice their Lego counterparts as well as the standard array of Lego hijinks.

This is a cute, family-friendly way to catch up or refresh your memory. It includes sections of The Mandalorian and The Book of Boba Fett, with the story bringing you to just before the start of the film. And since The Mandalorian and Grogu movie will hit Disney Plus the same day as its Lego preview, you can treat yourself to some giggles before locking in and enjoying the action-packed film right after. Just be careful with your wallet after, or you’ll end up with a shopping cart full of your own Star Wars Lego kits.

Tech.title: X-Men Cast, VisionQuest Trailer: All the Big Marvel News Out of D23
Tech.content:
Disney had a night packed with movie and streaming announcements, including the Star Wars: Starfighter trailer, Zootopia 3 and The Incredibles 3 reveals, the Frozen 3 trailer and so much more. But during the entertainment showcase on Friday night in Anaheim, there was also some big Marvel Cinematic Universe news.

Here are the biggest Marvel reveals from Disney’s D23 fan convention.

X-Men Cast revealed

The cast of X-Men was rounded out at D23. Corinne Reichert/CNET

The cast for the upcoming X-Men movie was finally announced, with Marvel chief Kevin Feige joined by Sadie Sink to bring them all out on stage. Sink plays Jean Grey — as revealed during Spider-Man: Brand New Day — and we also found out that alongside Kit Connor as Cyclops/Scott Summers and Samara Weaving as Emma Frost, we’ll get Christopher Abbott as Professor Charles Xavier, Inde Navarrette as Rogue and Maya Boyd as Ororo Munroe/Storm.

Adam Driver appeared via video link to tease that he would be playing Magneto, before eventually admitting he was cast as Nathaniel Milbury — one of the many names for X-Men villain Mr. Sinister.

The role of Storm has been an especially hot topic, with rumors flying for months on who would get the gig. Storm’s history with the X-Men and the Avengers is legendary, as the powerful weather-manipulating hero has fought plenty of battles alongside them, as part of the X-Men, and while apart from them. In the comics, she married the king of Wakanda and became queen, was part of the Secret Wars story as a minion of Doctor Doom and gained abilities from Asgard to become a Thor.

With such a seasoned track record in Marvel’s multiple stories and realities, once Storm is introduced to the MCU, it’s possible for her to show up anywhere. Given Sink’s Jean Grey’s appearance in Spider-Man: Brand New Day, the X-Men may show up in other MCU films, and are confirmed to be in the next big crossover film, Doomsday.

The X-Men film will hit the big screen on May 5, 2028.

Avengers: Doomsday trailer

Joining Feige on stage to introduce the Avengers: Doomsday trailer were Robert Downey Jr (Victor Von Doom), Chris Evans (back as Steve Rogers) and Hayley Atwell (Peggy Carter). They noted that the movie will feature not only the Avengers but also the Fantastic Four and the original X-Men.

The star-studded trailer included Victor Von Doom easily fighting off Chris Hemsworth’s Thor. The trailer ended with Doctor Doom raising Sentinel robots, which have been deployed against the X-Men in movies and comics.

We also saw glimpses of Simu Liu (Shang-Chi), Patrick Stewart (Professor X), Vanessa Kirby (Sue Storm) and Ian McKellan (Magneto) — and even Steve Rogers holding a baby.

Via video, Hugh Jackman (Wolverine), speaking to an off-stage Ryan Reynolds (Deadpool), also begged to be included in Avengers: Doomsday, but Feige didn’t make it sound as though that would be a possibility.

Avengers: Doomsday is out in cinemas on Dec. 18.

A trailer for VisionQuest

Aside from a trailer during Disney upfronts in May, we had yet to see footage from the new series starring Paul Bettany as Vision and James Spader as Ultron.

Bettany and Spader joined Feige to announce the VisionQuest trailer, which kicks off with Vision seeing a W+V heart carved into a table and looking quizzically at it. He has been reanimated and is watching old footage of himself from both Avengers and WandaVision, including his children, Billy and Tommy Maximoff (we last saw the kids in Agatha All Along, so we know they’re out there somewhere).

“In the Marvel universe, no one is ever really dead,” Bettany said. “What, or perhaps who, is he exactly? And what is it that makes us human?”

VisionQuest hits Disney Plus on Oct. 14.

Tech.title: Disney D23 Movies and Streaming Lineup: Biggest Surprises and Everything Else
Tech.content:
Disney’s biennial fan convention D23 is underway in Anaheim, and the entertainment giant hosted a star-studded entertainment showcase to unveil all upcoming movies and streaming shows, as well as trailers and sneak peeks of the ones we already know about.

Along with Frozen 3, The Incredibles 3, the Marvel reveals and all the Star Wars news, here are the biggest surprises and everything else announced on Friday night.

The Bluey movie: a keepy uppy teaser

A short teaser has finally been showcased for the upcoming feature film extension of the beloved Australian children’s show Bluey.

The brief trailer showed 3D-animated versions of Bluey and her sister Bingo playing their keepy uppy game, bouncing a balloon between each other until it hit the grass and they ran out of sight.

The teaser was very short, but the Bluey movie will be released a year from now, in Aug. 2027.

Creator Joe Brumm is stepping down from his role following the release of the movie, so for now, rewatching the first three seasons and the minisodes on Disney Plus is all we’ve got for the next year.

Zootopia 3 flies onto screens

Zootopia 3 was announced at Disney’s D23 streaming keynote. Corinne Reichert/CNET

It was a big day for Disney threequels as the third installment of the Zootopia franchise was a surprise announcement, coming less than a year after Zootopia 2 was released.

Birds will be the new addition to Zootopia 3, with a teaser showing a feather floating on the breeze through the animal-inhabited metropolis.

Ginnifer Goodwin as Judy Hopps and Ke Huy Quan as Gary De’Snake are confirmed to be returning for the third Zootopia movie.

Coco 2 announced

Coco 2 was announced at D23 and is scheduled to come out in Nov. 2029. Corinne Reichert/CNET

A sequel to the hugely popular 2017 Pixar film, Coco, was announced, with main character Miguel now a teenager, still playing music and still battling against former hero-turned-villain Ernesto de la Cruz.

Coco 2 will hit the big screen in Nov. 2029.

Kingdom Hearts IV release date and series

The Coco announcement also served as a segue into a trailer and release date for the fourth Kingdom Hearts game (late 2027), with Miguel’s world being added to the beloved franchise when it comes out.

Plus, a Kingdom Hearts cartoon series will be coming to Disney Plus “soon.”

First look at live-action Tangled

A sneak peek of the live-action version of the Disney film Tangled was shown by Kathryn Hahn during the D23 streaming keynote. Corinne Reichert/CNET

We got a brief teaser showing Teagan Croft as live-action Rapunzel, Milo Manheim as Flynn Rider and Kathryn Hahn as Mother Gothel, all in full costume.

Hahn, who thanked fans for manifesting her as the Tangled villain, appeared on stage at D23, introducing a video of Manheim and Croft detailing some of the filming locations across Spain where the movie is being shot, including monasteries and cathedrals.

Tangled will be released on March 31, 2028.

Percy Jackson season 3 gets a trailer

Ahead of its Nov. 20 release, Percy Jackson and the Olympians got a fresh, new trailer. Walker Scobell (Percy Jackson) was joined on stage by Ming-Na Wen (Hera) and Andra Day (Athena) to show off the new trailer.

Season 3 adapts the book The Titan’s Curse, and shows Percy fighting underwater and in arenas as a titan emerges.

Pixar’s Gatto trailers shows a cat among the pigeons

Two trailers for the Pixar film Gatto were seen at the D23 streaming keynote, with the movie scheduled to come out March 5, 2027. Corinne Reichert/CNET

Pixar’s next animated feature film, Gatto, features a little black cat voiced by Mark Ruffalo. Set in Venice, Italy, with the same filmmakers behind Luca, Nero the cat makes a pigeon friend who helps him escape the clutches of mob boss Rocco (Laurence Fishburne).

The pigeon gives him a bird’s-eye view of a Venetian square, and what obstacles to avoid or use to his advantage when attempting to close in on a violinist street performer.

A second trailer was shown, with Gatto, Rocco and dozens of other stray cats roaming the streets of Venice — which Gatto describes as “a sinking death trap” — and stealing fish.

Gatto will be released on March 5, 2027.

The New Simpsons Movie

The New Simpsons Movie had a very rough, sketched teaser shown at Disney’s D23 streaming keynote. Corinne Reichert/CNET

Season 38 of The Simpsons is about to kick off next month, but everyone’s favorite yellow cartoon family is also getting a second movie — two decades after the release of the first.

A “very rough” teaser was showcased during Disney’s biennial fan convention D23 in Anaheim on Friday night, featuring concept art sketches of Homer and his friends at a Springfield Isotopes baseball game.

Details are scant, but it looks like the Simpsons family and their friends will be back to their usual hijinks. The sketches showed Homer and all the beloved characters of the show rush to catch a ball as it bounced around all of Springfield before it got shot back to the stadium, where it landed right in front of Bart.

The New Simpsons Movie will be released on Sept. 3, 2027.

Hexed cast and trailer

A new Disney animated movie, Hexed, is coming soon. Corinne Reichert/CNET

Disney animated feature Hexed, which stars Hailee Steinfeld in the title role of teenager Billie who discovers she’s a witch, got a trailer and new casting news just months before it comes out on Thanksgiving weekend.

Steinfeld was joined on stage by Walton Goggins, who voices a three-eyed cat named Beef, and Jodie Foster, who voices the queen of witches.

The new trailer showed Billie getting sucked inside a crescent moon-shaped portal to a secret realm of magic, filled with spellbooks, talking objects, a magical forest and a coven of witches.

Ice Age: Boiling Point trailer – squirrels in lava

Queen Latifah and Denis Leary appeared at Disney’s D23 keynote to introduce another film in the Ice Age franchise. Corinne Reichert/CNET

Manny, Sid, Diego, Ellie and Peaches are back in a sixth theatrical Ice Age movie.

Queen Latifah (the voice of mammoth Ellie) and Dennis Leary (who voices saber-tooth tiger Diego) appeared on stage to introduce the first trailer for Ice Age: Boiling Point.

“We’re finishing up the movie right now, and it’s really funny and it’s scary,” Leary said.

The trailer showed squirrel Scrat and Baby Scrat pushing an acorn into the ice once more, but this time with the acorns falling through into the lava boiling below. Scrat rides the acorn through a sea of lava, until an enormous prehistoric squirrel grabs the prize at the end.

The trailer briefly shows Manny, Sid and Ellie exploring a jungle-like setting nearby.

Original Ice Age animator Blue Sky Studios was acquired by Disney in 2019 and shut down and absorbed five years ago. A short series featuring Scrat and Baby Scrat was released on Disney Plus in 2022.

Ice Age: Boiling Point will hit the big screen in less than a year, on Feb. 5, 2027.

Oswald miniseries on Disney Plus

Director and MCU godfather Jon Favreau appeared at Disney’s D23 streaming keynote to introduce Oswald, a limited miniseries coming to Disney Plus. Corinne Reichert/CNET

Disney director and producer Jon Favreau introduced his passion project, Oswald — an original character created by Walt Disney 100 years ago — that will air as a three-part miniseries on Disney Plus next year.

“We only used hand-drawn 2D animation for Oswald,” Favreau said, adding that many old Disney animators were brought back to work on the project.

In a Roger Rabbit-esque series, Oswald will feature live-action settings, including Walt’s old office in Burbank and at Disneyland, where the 2D-animated Oswald runs around and explores the real world.

Clay, a new Disney animated film

Clay will be the next original Disney animated feature film. Corinne Reichert/CNET

Disney’s newly announced animated featured film, Clay, will see Flip, a stinky skunk voiced by Kieran Culkin, forced to become a mentor to a literal chunk of clay.

Clay will be released in 2028.

Pixar’s Ghost Market

A mysterious new Pixar feature film called Ghost Market (which the teaser said would be about “hungry ghosts”) will be released in spring 2028.

Lilo and Stitch 2: live action

The Lilo and Stitch 2 live-action movie is announced. Corinne Reichert/CNET

Following the release of the live-action version of Lilo and Stitch, Disney has decided to continue by adapting the animated sequel into the live format. Lilo and Stitch 2 includes Angel, the pink, female version of the outer-space monster who debuted in the animated Lilo & Stitch: The Series.

Lilo and Stitch 2 live action will be released on May 28, 2028.

Romy and Michele 2

Lisa Kudrow and Mira Sorvino came on stage at Disney’s D23 streaming keynote to announce a sequel to their iconic film, Romy And Michele’s High School Reunion. Corinne Reichert/CNET

Back in 1997, Romy and Michele got together for their high school reunion. Now, 30 years later, Lisa Kudrow and Mira Sorvino reunited once more on stage to announce Romy and Michele 2.

The ladies wore modern versions of their outfits from the ’90s cult classic, talking about their boutique in Beverly Hills and another reunion on the horizon.

Camp Rock 3 live performance

The Jonas Brothers appeared on stage at Disney’s D23 streaming keynote to introduce the Camp Rock 3 live performance. Corinne Reichert/CNET

The Jonas Brothers appeared on stage to talk about the old days and introduce the new, leading to a live performance featuring the new stars of the fresh new movie in the Camp Rock series.

It premiered Aug. 14 on Disney Plus.

Tech.title: Patent Filing Suggests Meta’s Facial Recognition Glasses Are Coming
Tech.content:
A filing submitted by Meta to the US Patent and Trademark Office shows that Meta has continued developing features that use facial recognition in conjunction with its controversial smart glasses. The application for the patent was submitted in February and made public this week. There’s no indication of how long the approval process could take or whether the patent will ultimately be granted.

The application, which CNET has viewed, includes 44 pages of drawings and descriptions of a system that would use Meta’s smart glasses technology in conjunction with AI facial recognition. The system would use AI facial recognition to identify people and create media, including videos, that contain that information. It could also use inputs such as location data or information from online services to create those media files, support a wide range of content-creation activities or interact with Meta services, according to the lengthy filing.

A representative for Meta did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The patent filing comes at a sensitive time for Meta and this product category. Privacy advocates have heavily criticized the company’s lack of privacy protections, while the nickname “pervert glasses” has been used more frequently in media stories about its smart glasses.

That sentiment was expanded upon by the nonprofit Center for Democracy and Technology, which issued a statement about the patent application, calling it an escalation of privacy harms.

“Meta’s patent application includes relatively innocuous use cases, but, if deployed, this tech can and will be used for much more nefarious purposes and will put marginalized people like victims of stalking and domestic violence at risk,” wrote Ariana Aboulafia, project lead for disability rights in technology policy for the center.

“No one should be forced to constantly question whether the person next to them at a party, in the doctor’s office, or on the train is constantly recording, identifying, and storing information about them,” Aboulafia wrote.

How soon for these features?

Meta drew criticism after it distributed dormant facial‑recognition code within its Meta AI app, a move the company later reversed by removing the software entirely. It has also faced criticism for testing facial recognition software sold by a vendor that deals with military and police contracts.

Some of the backlash originated with an investigation from Wired, confirmed by the Electronic Frontier Foundation’s Threat Lab, which found hidden code that was distributed to all Meta AI app users. Those findings put Meta on the defensive, and the company lashed out at Wired for its coverage even as it rolled back that software.

Meta isn’t the only company that has been the target of increased public scrutiny over technology and privacy; Flock Safety has been countering bad publicity and vandalism as well as pausing or canceling contracts for its license plate reader cameras in cities, including Los Angeles and Dayton, Ohio. Flock’s technology has also been criticized for incidents in which law enforcement officers have misused the tech to track people; despite policy changes, there are many ways to circumvent its safeguards.

Tech.title: Disney Snuck In and Overhauled the Millennium Falcon While You Were Sleeping. Here’s Why
Tech.content:
When Disney announced back in May that Millennium Falcon: Smuggler’s Run in both Disneyland and Hollywood Studios was getting an update with new missions, it was widely viewed as a welcomed but fairly minor update to the popular attraction. At its D23 conference this weekend, Disney Imagineers are offering a deep dive into how that update happened and a peek behind the curtain at all the tools used to make that update a reality.

For the uninitiated, there’s quite a bit of sleight of hand involved in how Smuggler’s Run works. Each version of this ride has multiple cockpits that rotate around on a massive set of plates, so more people can quickly get on and off the ride. This means there are 28 iterations of the same ride environment inside both the California and Florida versions of the Star Wars: Galaxy’s Edge attraction. According to Disney Imagineers Asa Kalama and Angela Jay, each one of those 28 cockpits is powered by five 4K projectors driven by eight graphics cards to make the whole thing work.



The upgrade to Smuggler’s Run back in May added a lot of complexity to the ride, allowing riders to choose between different worlds to travel to for your unique adventure. To make something like that possible, every single one of the 224 graphics cards was upgraded to a new Nvidia Blackwell card and the whole game was updated to Unreal Engine 5. This allowed the platform as a whole to be more flexible, but it also allowed the testing environment to get an upgrade as well.

A big part of the Imagineering Pavilion at D23 this year is dedicated to a live demo of the developer console used to test Smuggler’s Run and its many new updates. This includes virtual buttons to simulate all the functions in the cockpit, screens dedicated to all the readouts you see while on the ride and, of course, multiple perspectives of the game itself.

Some testing is done within virtual reality headsets so they can see the same way you would by sitting in the ride, while other times people are sat in an office with a phone or tablet that has all the buttons laid out. Nearly all of it happens on a computer just like the one in the ride to make sure everyone gets the same experience.

One other important thing to know about Smuggler’s Run is how incredibly popular it is. If you’re a regular in either theme park, you know this ride always has a line, and nobody likes it when a popular ride is offline, even if it’s for very cool upgrades. That’s why Imagineers set off working overnight for weeks to successfully update the hardware and the software for this ride, and the result was zero downtime.

It’s clear from the way Kalama and Jay talked about the work on Smuggler’s Run in 2026 that more is coming for the most famous hunk of junk in the galaxy. It’s clear this work wasn’t just for helping the Mandalorian and Grogu take out Imperials, as made clear by a new partnership with Fortnite where your gameplay in Smuggler’s Run will carry over. This ride has now not only been future-proofed for more upgrades later on, but the success of what seemed at first like a fairly minor update to the software likely means Smuggler’s Run will be able to feel new and interesting for years. If you’re not sure why that’s important, remember that Indiana Jones in Disneyland is still running Windows XP.

Tech.title: Starfighter Trailer, Ahsoka and Anakin: Biggest Star Wars News Out of D23
Tech.content:
Live at the Honda Center in Anaheim on Friday night as part of Disney’s D23 fan convention, Lucasfilm President Dave Filoni announced some of what’s coming next in the Star Wars universe.

And perhaps the biggest reveal was a trailer for the upcoming film, Starfighter.

Starfighter

Corinne Reichert/CNET

Disney’s D23 event gave fans a peek at the new chapter in the Star Wars franchise during its entertainment presentation on Friday, revealing a trailer for Lucasfilm’s Star Wars: Starfighter film. The movie was announced in early 2025 and is due to hit theaters on May 28, 2027. The film features Ryan Gosling and Flynn Gray portraying the lead characters.

Gosling, in a jacket with a skull and crossbones, was on hand to reveal fresh details about his upcoming Star Wars film. The emblem is the signature of his character, whose name was revealed to be Kade Auberon — not one franchise fans should recognize, but certainly one that sounds like it came from a galaxy far, far away.

Gosling called it a life-changing role before introducing the trailer.

Set five years after the events of 2019’s The Rise of Skywalker, the space-faring tale teases Gosling riding “the fastest starfighter ever built.”

Gosling plays a talented pilot, while Gray is the young boy he’s charged to protect. The packed cast also includes Aaron Pierre, Mia Goth, Amy Adams, Daniel Ings, Jamael Westman, Simon Bird and House of the Dragon’s Matt Smith.

Shawn Levy is directing the adventure flick. At the Star Wars Celebration in Japan last year, he explained how this story is in a lane of its own. “This is a stand-alone,” he said. “It’s not a prequel, not a sequel. It’s a new adventure. It’s set in a period of time that we haven’t seen explored yet.”

It’ll hit theaters on May 28, 2027.

Ahsoka season 2: Hayden Christensen is back as Anakin

Corinne Reichert/CNET

Joining Filoni on stage were Ahsoka live-action actress Rosario Dawson; Eman Esfandi, who plays Ezra Bridger; and, surprisingly, Hayden Christensen, who played Anakin Skywalker in Star Wars Episodes II and III.

Anakin was a big part of the original Ahsoka Tano story in the animated Clone Wars series, and Christensen’s return to the character in a pivotal episode during the first season of Ahsoka was arguably its best. It makes sense for him to return in season two, seemingly in flashbacks of Ahsoka’s past and as a guiding Force ghost in her present.

The teaser trailer showed Christensen leading Ahsoka to, perhaps, become a Jedi once again.

Ahsoka season 2 will stream on Disney Plus on Jan 20, 2027.

Star Wars IV coming back to theaters

To celebrate the 50th anniversary of Star Wars, which was released in 1977, the original movie will be rereleased in its original form in theaters next year.
